articles.title: Akash to Pralay: Why private missile manufacturing could be a game changer for India's defence readiness
articles.summary: News News: In a landmark push toward expanding self-reliance in defence manufacturing, the Centre has approved the transfer of Defence Research and Development O.
articles.body: In a landmark push toward expanding self-reliance in defence manufacturing, the Centre has approved the transfer of Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)-developed technologies for all conventional missile systems to the Indian private industry. This has marked one of the most significant shifts in India's missile production model. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh cleared the decision, allowing qualified domestic companies to move beyond mere component supply and undertake full-scale, in-house production of missile systems for the first time.The conventional portfolio being thrown open is extensive, which according to sources covers Akash family of surface-to-air missiles, Very Short Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS), missiles of the Astra air-to-air family, Rudram anti-radiation missile, anti-tank systems including Nag and SANT, Man-Portable ATGM (MP-ATGM), Naval Anti-Ship Missile-Short Range (NASM-SR), Long Range Land-Attack Cruise Missiles (LR-LACM) and Pralay quasi-ballistic missile. Strategic missiles such as the Agni series and the K-series will not be made by the private industry. Weapons such as the Brahmos and the Medium Range Surface to Air Missile (MRSAM), jointly developed by Russia and Israel respectively, as they are governed by separate arrangements.This marks a clear departure from the decades-old model where DRDO handed over its missile designs almost exclusively to state-run Bharat Dynamics Limited for series production. Going forward, private firms will compete for technology licences through a bidding process, opening the field to companies such as Tata, Adani, Bharat Forge, Mahindra and ICOMM, all of whom are already contracted for various tactical missile and rocket programmes. The defence ministry states that the shift will strengthen the domestic industrial base, cut import dependence, boost MSME participation, and raise indigenous value addition, cementing India's transition from being primarily an importer to becoming a serious player in the global missile export market.DRDO-private industry partnership on the riseThe Development-cum-Production Partner (DcPP) model has quietly become one of the most consequential frameworks in India's push for self-reliance in defence manufacturing. Conceived by DRDO, it works on a simple principle, capable manufacturing partners are identified from both public and private sectors through competitive selection, and the technology needed to actually produce these systems is then transferred to them.The scale of this ecosystem is striking. DRDO now draws on a network of over 2,200 industries capable of producing sub-systems, systems and equipment. By March this year, 134 companies had signed on as DcPPs or Production Agencies, more than 2,180 technology transfer agreements had been inked, and upwards of 2,780 Intellectual Property Rights had been opened up for tthe private industry to use, till June this year. This marks a structural shift for a sector once concentrated almost entirely within public sector giants, where cutting-edge research often took years to reach the battlefield. The DcPP model has quietly built the industrial backbone behind India's broader defence manufacturing expansion.Why involving private industry mattersRecent and ongoing conflicts, such as those underway in Ukraine and in west Asia have demonstrated the importance of maintaining a significant weapons stockpile and the manufacturing capability to make these weapons at scale. The ability of private industry to manufacture these weapons at scale. The government's decision to transfer DRDO's conventional missile technologies to the private industry carries a clear set of advantages for the country's defence manufacturing sector. It allows missile systems to move directly from the drawing board into industrial-scale production, cutting the years-long lag that has often kept indigenous designs stuck at the prototype stage. It also breaks the near-monopoly enjoyed by state-run Bharat Dynamics Limited, whose production lines are already stretched thin by both domestic orders and a growing export pipeline.By opening the field to multiple qualified private players, the decision widens India's overall manufacturing capacity, while also pulling MSMEs deeper into the supply chain rather than restricting participation to large conglomerates alone. This, in turn, is expected to push up domestic value addition and reduce dependence on imported components, a long-standing weak point in India's defence ecosystem.Crucially, the move also builds surge capacity, giving India the industrial depth to scale up output quickly should a prolonged conflict demand it, while strengthening the country's hand in a defence export market where interest in systems like the Astra is already growing. For DRDO itself, offloading production duties frees up bandwidth to focus squarely on developing the next generation of weapons systems.Private missile production in IndiaEven before this week's technology transfer announcement, Indian private industry had already built a substantial missile manufacturing footprint. Tata Advanced Systems has been central to the Akash Air Force Launcher programme and produces MRSAM Army launchers mounted on its own HMV 8x8 vehicles, alongside supplying Pinaka rocket launchers and command posts under a two-decade public-private partnership with DRDO.Bharat Forge, through its subsidiary Kalyani Strategic Systems, has secured large Pinaka rocket contracts, including export orders to Armenia, and has been positioned as a serious contender for future strategic projects. Solar Defence and Aerospace has gone furthest in developing its own systems outright, the Nagastra loitering munition, used during Operation Sindoor, the Bhargavastra anti-drone salvo system, and the proposed Maheshwarastra precision rocket family, besides serving as production agency for guided Pinaka rockets.Adani Defence and Aerospace has developed the SR-1 loitering munition and VTOL-5 attack drone in-house, while also acting as a DRDO production partner for guided munitions and anti-radiation missiles. ICOMM Tele contributes missile guidance systems and sub-components, while Mahindra Defence's missile-adjacent work remains largely confined to naval systems such as torpedo launchers and anti-submarine suites, rather than missiles themselves. Adani also lists weapon systems such as VSHORAD, MR-SAM, Rudram-1 and UAV Launched Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM) on its website.

articles.title: A San Francisco woman hires a humanoid robot for $30 an hour to clean her apartment while controlling it remotely from her sofa
articles.summary: US News: A San Francisco woman has given a glimpse of what home cleaning could look like in the age of humanoid robots after hiring one for $30 an hour to work.
articles.body: A San Francisco woman has given a glimpse of what home cleaning could look like in the age of humanoid robots after hiring one for $30 an hour to work inside her apartment. Gianna Capezio booked a one-hour cleaning visit from San Francisco startup Tau Robotics, with the humanoid robot vacuuming, making her bed and cleaning her bathroom during the session. The robot was not operating autonomously. A trained human operator controlled it remotely through its cameras, with artificial intelligence assisting the system. Capezio said the robot was slower than a human cleaner but still did a solid job and she did not have to redo its work afterwards. Her video of the unusual cleaning session quickly spread online, attracting millions of views and sparking debate over the technology, its usefulness and the future of household work.San Francisco woman hires a humanoid robot for a $30 cleaning visitCapezio's experience came after Tau Robotics began offering its humanoid cleaning service to selected customers in San Francisco. The company currently operates the service on an invite-only basis, with customers paying a flat $30 for a one-hour visit. Tau advertises its robots for tasks including vacuuming, wiping surfaces, taking out rubbish and clearing light clutter, while its current service also offers options for kitchen, bathroom and deeper cleaning. Customers cannot simply leave the robot alone inside an empty property. Tau's terms require the customer or another authorised adult to remain at home throughout the visit, and the company does not accept keys, lockboxes or door codes. The robot also depends on a working internet connection and electricity because it is operated remotely. The service is therefore still an early-stage experiment rather than a conventional autonomous cleaning business, but it represents a notable step because a humanoid machine is now being sent into real homes to perform paid household work.A human operator controls the robot remotelyThe most important part of Tau's system is that the humanoid is not yet capable of independently cleaning an entire home. Tau's own terms state that the robot is operated in real time by a trained human operator working from the company's facility, while AI assists with the robot's operation. Tau says its robots are jointly operated by humans and AI, with the balance between direct human control and higher-level guidance varying depending on the task. The company's long-term objective is to reduce that dependence and eventually have its robots perform more of the work autonomously. That makes the current service different from a fully independent household robot. A person is effectively guiding the machine while the customer watches it carry out physical tasks inside the home. The approach also allows Tau to gather information from real cleaning sessions that can be used to improve its AI models. articles.title: How Stephen Curry played a huge role in Golden State Warriors’ first new signing of the offseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors spent over two months of the 2026 offseason without signing a single new player to their roster before finally making an addition o...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors spent over two months of the 2026 offseason without signing a single new player to their roster before finally making an addition on August 25.

The Warriors spent most of their offseason recruiting LeBron James , a pursuit that failed. The team has been quiet since then, but made two late-August signings to bolster their roster before the season.

Guard Brandon Williams and forward Georges Niang both signed on minimum contracts with the franchise, with Stephen Curry specifically playing a crucial role in one of them joining the Warriors.

Stephen Curry recruited new signing Brandon Williams on a Zoom call

The SF Chronicle spoke to Toby Spino, Williams' coach and advisor, and revealed that Curry pitched Brandon on joining the Warriors a few months ago.

"Golden State has had a target on Williams for months. Earlier this summer… Stephen Curry set up a call with Williams to talk shop. 'When he first came in, he was like, 'Oh, I gotta go home. I got a Zoom call with Wardell.'"

Despite the call being months ago, Williams was left in a state of limbo as the Warriors were in the middle of their LeBron pursuit at the time.

Now, after a summer of primarily bringing back the roster that missed the playoffs last season, Williams became the Warriors' first addition of the summer, beating Georges Niang to that honor by a few hours.

Williams will be a backup rotational guard for the Warriors behind Curry and De'Anthony Melton. While his role depends on how the season plays out, this is a high-upside signing by GSW.

Brandon Williams' 2025-26 stats before joining the Warriors

Williams averaged 13.0 points and 3.9 assists on 47.2% from the field and 23.2% from three for the Mavericks last season.

He is a true NBA developmental story, going undrafted but staying on a two-way contract with the Mavericks for multiple seasons before finally getting a breakout opportunity last season.

His poor three-point shooting held the Mavericks back from extending him and warded off other teams looking for low-usage rotational players to stretch the floor.

The Warriors have enough floor-spacing and need genuine driving threats from the perimeter who can collapse defenses while also having the scoring touch to create their own opportunities.

Williams is also an above-average defender despite being 6'2″, primarily due to his hustle and intensity. He's a great rotational fit for the Warriors and could have a breakout season if his shot has improved, given that the Warriors have opportunities for guards like him to come in and succeed.

articles.title: Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test live win probability, scorecard, chances of victory in Colombo
articles.summary: Track Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test live win probability, full scorecard, updates, and real-time victory chances from the SSC Ground in Colombo.
articles.body:
The India-Sri Lanka series shifts venues for its decider, moving from Galle's spin-friendly track to the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo, which is a ground known for offering a very different kind of contest.

Batting first has historically paid off at this venue, with teams regularly posting big totals early in matches, which makes Wednesday's toss potentially decisive.

MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS

Rain looms as a genuine concern too, with forecasts suggesting interruptions across all five days, while Colombo's heat is expected to sap energy from the bowling attacks. Spin has still had the upper hand recently, as spinners have picked up 45 wickets across the last three Tests here, compared to 35 for the pacers.

India arrive full of confidence following their commanding 165-run win in the series opener. Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, and Manav Suthar were the standout contributors in Galle. They will fancy their chances of completing a 2-0 sweep, a result that would also strengthen their push toward the 2027 World Test Championship final.

Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source

Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test: Toss result & live updates

India are eight wickets away from wrapping this up, while Sri Lanka still trail by 130 to make the visitors bat a second time. The surface isn't misbehaving wildly, but there's just enough bite in it to keep every batter on edge.

The key figure for Sri Lanka is 111.4, which is the total overs India's attack has bowled over the last couple of days. If the hosts can stitch together a couple of stubborn stands here, tired legs might finally start catching up with the bowlers.

Pasindu Sooriyabandara has looked sharp once again, currently unbeaten on 35. At the other end, Kamindu Mendis is desperate to sign off from a quiet series with a substantial knock. Plenty of pride on the line for this batting group.

We'll be right back with the afternoon session shortly.

Sri Lanka couldn't dodge the follow-on after all. Dinusha edged one off Manav Suthar, and KL Rahul made no mistake, pouching a clean catch in the slips to wrap things up.

With that wicket, India wasted no time telling the hosts to pad up again. They've enforced the follow-on, sending Sri Lanka straight back out to the middle.

Sonal Dinusha reaches his century with a smacking boundary off Prasidh Krishna! SL still need 21 more to avoid a follow-on.

Sri Lanka lost six wickets as Manav Suthar and Prasidh Krishna ran through the hosts batting lineup. The duo of Dinusha and Kumara remain unbeaten at the end of Day 3 with the all-rounder once again becoming Sri Lanka's saviour.

Suthar looks for his back-to-back five-wicket hauls while Dinusha looks to be a centurion once again.

Sri Lanka are still 87 runs short of avoiding a follow-on as India continue to enjoy the upper hand.

Pasindu departs for 80 runs after a brilliant knock as Sri Lanka are now staring at follow-on.

After the setback at the end of Day 2, the hosts show great fight in the first session as the cross the 100-run mark.

Sri Lanka resume fight to save the match

The hosts were in trouble at the end of Day 2 of the series decider in Colombo. Sri Lankan batters will hope to bat all through day 3 to stand a chance of saving the game.

A bit of drama to close out a rain-hit Day 2. Dhruv Jurel's gritty hundred pushed India past the 500-run mark before the skipper called the declaration. Play had already lost a solid two hours to bad weather earlier, and the rain returned to eat into Sri Lanka's reply as well.

When they did get on the park, Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar ripped through with a wicket apiece, leaving the hosts reeling at 8/2 before stumps.

It took a tense 22 deliveries to move from 99 to three figures, but Dhruv Jurel finally got across the line to seal his second Test hundred. In the end, he didn't need anything flashy, just a firm push to mid-off that kicked up off the deck, giving him just enough daylight to scramble through.

He still had to put in a full-stretch dive to make his ground, and a direct hit might've made it tight. The throw missed, though, and Jurel could finally exhale. India declare at 503.

A quick drizzle forced India to take an early tea as the covers came down to cover the pitch. Sri Lanka controlled the runs this innings, with Mohammad Siraj leaving it to Jurel to take the shots.

Back from lunch, the hosts were able to remove the explosive Pant and Manav Suthar in quick succession to bring some respite to Sri Lanka. Jurel, meanwhile, continues to hold India's innings, batting at 81* and looking for his second international ton.

With Jurel and Pant both dominating the Sri Lankan pace attack, the hosts would look for their spinners to bring the swing on the old ball. The duo quickly put on a 100-run partnership, with Jurel scoring his second 50 of the series.

Meanwhile, his batting companion would be looking for that elusive 9th century as a keeper to go clear of England's Les Ames.

Twin half-centuries from Jurel and a returning Rishabh Pant have allowed the visitors to breach the 400-run mark. Pant, in particular, has played with his characteristic gusto, bagging his second 50+ score of the series while his batting companion Jurel is matching his play stroke by stroke.

Sri Lanka gets an early breakthrough on day 2 as Asitha Fernando bags his fourth wicket by dismissing Saransh Jain. The debutant tried to go for a flick, but the ball pops up on his left and lands straight at Kamil Mishara at the gully.

India ends day 1 with 300 runs on the board and half their batters back to the dressing room. Asitha Fernando remained the dominant bowler for the hosts taking three scalps including Gill and Jaiswal.

Sri Lanka would hope to quickly dismiss the visitors come day 2.

Padikkal's marathon stay finally ended on 117 from 193 balls, bowled by Keshara Nuwantha in the over before the second new ball became available. It was a soft way to go; the left-hander pushed back rather than forward to a quicker, flatter delivery that gripped, turned past the outside edge and crashed into the off stump.

Jadeja and Padikkal have picked up where Pant left off, ticking the score along without any alarms. The left-hander reached his second Test century in the space of a week, getting there off 168 balls with a single eased down to long-on, and celebrated by removing his helmet to acknowledge the dressing room.

He had moved into the nineties in style, backing away to hammer Jayasuriya through cover before flashing another cut through the same region. Sri Lanka's bowlers, already warned once for a slow over rate, are running out of ideas in the Colombo heat.

Rishabh Pant has been forced to leave the pitch after being hit on his left forearm. The Indian wicketkeeper was visibly in pain as he walked off the pitch. Pant's misfortune with injuries continues.

Padikkal got a huge reprieve off the very first ball, but since then he has looked like a man on a mission. He has brought up his 50 with a well-timed drive wide of cover. It started as a call for a double before he looked up and saw it had raced away to the rope.

At the other end, Shubman Gill has notched up his half-century as well. But a reckless shot at a ball outside off stump and he has to walk back.

So far so good for India. Gill and Padikkal have been playing risk-free cricket and yet managing to get the runs. The half-century partnership arrived off 96 balls. The pitch still has a bit of spice for the quicks, but they've hardly bowled. The sweltering heat in Colombo probably isn't helping.

A couple of wickets down, a couple of catches down, and a helmet-butt from Jaiswal, and it was an eventful morning session. India are still scoring above 3.5 rpo, but Gill & Padikkal would be cautious when they come out in the second session.

A watchful beginning by the home side. The Sri Lankan fast bowlers are posing tough questions up front, and both KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal have had uncomfortable moments with the ball darting sharply back off the seam.

Toss: India won the toss and will bat first.

Sri Lanka vs India 2nd Test: Predicted playing XI

India predicted playing XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Shubman Gill(c), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant(w), Ravindra Jadeja, Dhruv Jurel, Kuldeep Yadav, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna

Sri Lanka predicted playing XI: Lahiru Udara, Nishan Madushka, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva(c), Sonal Dinusha, Niroshan Dickwella(w), Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando

articles.title: Joshua Zirkzee Key To Man Utd Transfers As Interest Remains
articles.summary: Joshua Zirkzee’s potential return to Italy holds the key to Manchester United’s recruitment plans as Michael Carrick targets a new striker to solve his side'...
articles.body:
Why Man United have always needed a striker this summer.

On the field, Manchester United could not have had a worse start to the season, with a 2-0 loss to newly-promoted Hull City.

In almost every regard, the Tigers outperformed the Red Devils, which will leave Michael Carrick with many tactical headaches.

Off the field, United could be braced for a very busy week with the transfer deadline on the 1st of September on the horizon.

In terms of incomings, Carlos Baleba has now completed his move from Brighton and Hove Albion . His first words as a Manchester United player can be found here .

Outgoings could be key for United if they want to bring in more players, as the futures of some senior squad and academy players are pivotal to the club.

Joshua Zirkzee has been linked with a move away all summer, with the same Serie A clubs hovering around the player but yet to make a formal offer. However, with the transfer deadline approaching, a deal may be more likely to advance.

According to Laurie Whitwell, the likes of Juventus and Como have shown clear interest in bringing the Dutchman back to Italy , where he excelled at Bologna .

He also reported that three other unnamed Premier League clubs are interested in him. One of those clubs could be Aston Villa , with the Midlands club looking for a striker and having previously been linked with the centre forward.

The departure of Zirkzee is so important because Whitwell also suggested that if the Dutchman did leave, the club could return to the market for a striker to deputise for or compete with Benjamin Sesko .

Lisandro Martinez's Suddenly 'Fighting' To Save Career Amid Man Utd Hierarchy DoubtsPersistent injury woes may force Manchester United to offload Lisandro Martinez, as club officials demand the Argentine proves his fitness before the summer transfer window shuts.

Zirkzee is undoubtedly a good footballer with a lot of talent, but the Dutchman has failed to adapt to life at Old Trafford, meaning a departure is best for all parties.

Against Hull City and at times last season, it was abundantly clear that without a real focal point up front, the team looked lost. While Matheus Cunha (who started up front against Hull), Bryan Mbeumo , and Marcus Rashford can play there, they lack the instincts and presence of an out-and-out striker.

When Sesko came on against Hull, it was clear that the impact of having a player consistently making those runs, even if the players could not find him, was hugely beneficial.

Whether it is an experienced player like Jean-Philippe Mateta or a riskier option like the youthful Nicolò Tresoldi , a striker is needed.

articles.title: Oosterwolde’s entourage confident player will pass medical
articles.summary: Roma was ready to welcome Jayden Oosterwolde to Trigoria yesterday. The Dutchman arrived in Rome this morning, landing at Ciampino Airport on a flight from A...
articles.body:
Roma was ready to welcome Jayden Oosterwolde to Trigoria yesterday.

The Dutchman arrived in Rome this morning, landing at Ciampino Airport on a flight from Amsterdam to begin his Giallorossi adventure.

However, the 2001-born defender had some trouble passing his medical.

As is well known, the Fenerbahçe defender is struggling with an injury, and the Giallorossi club wants to have a clear picture before adding the player to their squad. Today, Roma will decide whether to sign Oosterwolde or take a step back.

The deal, if necessary, will be concluded on a one-off loan worth €1 million with a €15 million option to buy, which could become a mandatory buyout with 15 appearances of 45 minutes each. On the player side, optimism is filtering through.

According to Matteo Moretto, those managing the 2001-born player's interests have leaked that the most likely scenario is for the deal to go through, despite the additional medical tests scheduled for today. Roma's final decision, however, remains dependent on the medical verdict.

articles.title: What happens when an athlete has a life-changing accident?
articles.summary: Saffron Cresswell was a promising eventer before a fall left her paralysed. Just eight months after first sitting in a canoe, she is heading to the Worlds.
articles.body:
After four months in hospital, Saffron Cresswell was dreading coming home.

Before she had the fall that would leave her paralysed at the age of 23, she had 25 horses that she trained and rode in a business she had been running since she was 15 and was a talented eventer on a pathway towards the Olympics.

Eight years earlier her parents had sold their house to buy a yard to support her career, with the family living in two tiny touring caravans for six years before they converted part of a barn into a home.

For years, Cresswell had been up at 5am, riding four ponies before school, then more afterwards - if she even went in. She puts her school attendance at "68% or something ridiculous" because she was "so busy riding".

'Busy' in fact turns out to be a common theme with Cresswell. During rehab at the hospital, she'd be waiting outside the gym for it to open so she could get an hour in before her physio session was even due to start.

There had only been five days during the four months where she hadn't had a visitor and so when she finally returned home to Worcestershire, where the horses had all been sold, reality was anything but hectic.

"I came home and fundamentally the next day, both my parents went out the door and went to work," says the now 25-year-old Cresswell. "So, I was home alone in a house that I couldn't really get out of and I couldn't really do anything."

There was only one thing for it: find a new sport. Little did she know that within eight months of sitting in a canoe for the first time, she would be heading for a World Championships.

Cresswell started riding when she was three, introduced to the sport by her mum, who was "horsey" but "doing low-level amateur stuff".

"I was the only child at primary school that was allowed a phone because I used to cycle from my primary school to the yard so I could start riding before my mum came home from work," she says.

She got into eventing "properly" at 13 when she produced her own young pony from beginners level to eventually representing Great Britain at three European championships.

She glances at the medals on her wall, saying: "One gold and two team silvers... so that sort of sparked the whole eventing career."

Then came the leap of faith from her parents - "much to my poor brother's trauma who was not horsey in any way" and was suddenly now sharing a caravan with his older sister - and Cresswell began running the business of riding and competing horses for other people and coaching.

Since her accident, she has not been back on a horse. Nor does she intend to.

"Because I'd done it so seriously and to such a high level that every day was about perfecting my technique and being better, I think, to get back on and not be able to do that physically, but also not even feel the horse underneath me, I think it would just be very disheartening for me," she says.

Instead, she coaches, which she says has helped her with what has turned out - surprisingly to her - the thing she would miss the most about pre-accident life.

"[What I miss] is literally just having the horse on the yard, to just go and like say 'hello' to them over the stable," she says. "And that comes from somebody who was so busy that I didn't really have loads of time to do that anyway."

The coaching is one of the new parts of the family business, which has had to change since her accident.

"The business is basically having to diversify, which is still very much an ongoing process," she says.

"My parents had given up so much to build something that allowed me to do the sport. It wasn't like we were at home and I left home and did this - they were very invested as well. So it's kind of affected everybody from that side of things."

Cresswell had been beginning to make her mark at senior level when she was competing at Bramham Horse Trials on 8 June, 2024.

Three fences before the end of her under-25 cross-country round, she came off her horse Vivendi Hero.

"I remember all of it because I didn't even get knocked out," she says. "[It was] just a freak accident.

"I just landed on the back of my head and unfortunately broke my back at T4 level - so chest level - and basically as soon as I fell, instantly knew I couldn't feel my legs."

She remembers an "awful" 45-minute ambulance ride to Leeds General Infirmary, where she had emergency surgery.

At that point, she wondered whether the damage would be permanent, because only couple of weeks previously she had been chatting to a friend - Olympic silver medallist Nicola Wilson - who had broken her neck in a fall.

"She said, 'when I fell, I couldn't feel my arm for 20 minutes, and then my feeling came back'. So when I had my accident, I had this really weird thing, like I just thought, 'oh, it's fine, it'll be 20 minutes, and my feeling will come back'," she says.

Wilson, who visited Cresswell in intensive care, regained her feeling in her legs in three or four weeks.

"So I have this really weird thing because then I was sort of waiting for three to four weeks as if I was going to get feeling back," says Cresswell, who was moved to a spinal unit in Wakefield.

"It was probably not until about six weeks that the realisation really hits... that actually this wasn't going to be the outcome that I had hoped for."

Cresswell was bedbound for six weeks in what she calls her "hotel room", a private room in the hospital where the wall was covered in get-well-soon cards.

Even then, she kept busy as the physios would give her some weights she could use for her arms.

"They were tiny, but in my head, it was a principle of having something to do every day," she says.

One of the first parts of rehab was learning to sit up again.

"With a spinal injury your blood pressure gets really lowered. So I couldn't sit up in a wheelchair for longer than about five minutes without feeling faint," says Cresswell.

Then there were things like putting on socks or tying up her hair, although even by the time she left hospital she still could not do the latter while sitting up because she did not have any core strength or balance.

She remembers her timetable at the unit - official physio was 2pm til 3pm but she would be at the gym when it opened at 1pm, having also been at the physio room at 10am when that opened.

She was determined to keep busy - and creative about how to make that happen.

Take, for example, when she was told that it would take too many people to help her swim.

"Instead of saying anything, I just used to say OK, that's fine, but can I come and sit and watch? So, I was basically just making myself known by the swimming pool," says Cresswell, who credits her athlete's mindset for her drive and ability to take positives from every situation.

"So, I went for two weeks. I sat and watched these other people in the physios do swimming.

"And funnily enough, by the third week, they thought, 'we're going to have to let her go in the swimming pool now because she's just going to annoy us otherwise'."

It turned out, water was going to become a huge part of her life.

Around a week before she left the spinal unit, Cresswell attended the Spinal Games at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, which is for patients with spinal injuries who are either still in hospital or within a year post-accident, and is an opportunity to try different sports over four days.

"I got six out of six bull's eyes and won the archery out of 110 people," she says.

"It was a great stepping stone to coming home. And I think I kind of held on to that when I came home initially because the first while was really tough at home."

She left hospital on 8 October and by December had started wheelchair racing, going on to race 10Ks and a half-marathon, also doing wheelchair tennis and basketball.

"I was worried I would never find a sport that I wanted to put my whole energy into," she says. "I think I knew that horses were my hobby that got to turn into my sport and my career and lifestyle so I didn't know if that would be possible to find something like that."

Cresswell had got chatting to Olympic canoe athlete Deborah Kerr at an event run by the Women's Sport Trust charity who had told her to "have a go".

So, on 23 December last year, she did. Winter was "not the time to start a water sport" and she was "not a natural".

"My coach was too scared to let me off the bank in case I capsized," she laughs. "And that probably stayed, I don't think I left the bank for about a month."

A one-off taster session turned into twice a week and then eventually five times a week on the water. Four-hour training sessions, plus gym work three days a week.

One of the biggest challenges has been staying upright.

"I don't have any feedback of any part of my body if I am losing balance," she explains. "So I'm strapped into a seat because I've got no core function, but I can't actually feel that seat. So I basically feel like I'm floating.

"So my only thing I've got to know if I've lost balance is my head and my eyes. So that took a while to start to hone in and they always say, deaf people hear better than anybody else, don't they? And I think it's a bit the same.

"It's like, I've now tuned into how to balance myself without the use of the rest of my body. But I'd say the balance aspect is a big part of it alongside the technical, constant skill-based stuff that needs to be improved."

It is the technical aspect that she thinks has similarities to equestrian and which is why she thinks she enjoys it so much.

Her progress has been rapid, by anyone's standards. Not least her own.

"World Championships was definitely not the plan. It was a quiet goal after a while that if I could get the time, I might be able to go," says Cresswell, who alongside training is also doing media work.

"The time I needed to achieve was, I think, one minute 26 seconds. And anyway, I'm now down to one minute 18. So I've kind of over-achieved on that one, which has just been through repetition, practise, finding new ways to do things."

She has been selected to represent Great Britain at this month's Canoe Sprint and Para-Canoe World Championships in Poznan, Poland.

Having only ever raced once before in the UK her aims are modest.

"Honestly, stay up and get through the start and finish line," she says, explaining that she capsized before the start of a race she was due to do in April.

It is more about getting an international classification - which involves a series of medical tests to assess an athlete's impairment and demonstrating how much of your body you can use when paddling - so that she can be eligible to earn points at events that can lead to qualification for the 2028 Paralympics in Los Angeles.

Could she have pictured this when she was in hospital?

"I certainly wouldn't have imagined I was going to do para-canoe - I didn't even know [that] was a sport when I was in hospital," says Cresswell, who will compete in the VL1 (a canoe with a support float) and KL1 (kayak).

"But to be honest, I think what actually is more kind of crazy in my head is I couldn't even imagine January me doing this."

articles.title: Duke Champion Kyle Singler Calls Out Coach K in Alarming Videos
articles.summary: Former Duke star Kyle Singler named Coach K directly in three concerning videos, accusing his former coach of setting him up while pleading for help. The pos...
articles.body:
Former Duke star Kyle Singler directly accused Mike Krzyzewski of mistreating him and repeatedly pleaded with his former coach for help across three concerning new social media videos.

"Coach K has set me up," Singler says in one of the videos. "Set me up, man."

Singler, the Most Outstanding Player of Duke's 2010 national championship run under Krzyzewski, makes a series of serious and sometimes difficult-to-follow allegations throughout the clips. He claims people have broken into his home, taken money and compromised his accounts, while repeatedly saying he feels unable to leave his residence.

The videos provide no evidence establishing those allegations as fact.

What they do make clear is whom Singler wants to hear his message.

"Coach, where you at?" Singler says. "Help my brother out. Thought we on the same team, man."

Singler's first video is centered largely on Krzyzewski, who coached him for all four of his seasons at Duke.

"I have no power. I have no house," Singler says. "I've reached out to coach and everybody has turned the other way."

Singler then alleges that his power has been cut off and that people have broken into his house, stolen money and ruined his life.

"Reached out to Coach K," Singler says. "And all he did is sit me on the bench."

It isn't clear what Singler means by being put on the bench. Krzyzewski retired from coaching Duke following the 2021-22 season, more than a decade after Singler's college career ended.

Neither Krzyzewski nor Duke appears to have publicly responded to Singler's latest statements.

Singler Also Makes Accusation Involving Duke

The second video contains another direct appeal to his former coach and expands Singler's claims to Duke.

Singler says he has experienced confrontations while living in Oklahoma and claims he feels unable to leave his home.

"Coach, I need your help," he says. "Help, man. I'm stuck at my house and I can't leave. I feel imprisoned."

Singler later says his "life's on the line" and alleges that people are breaking into his home and accounts and taking money.

"Duke's all about it," Singler says. "I got Duke again begging for my money. Everybody's after my money, trying to kill me."

Those are Singler's allegations, and the videos do not establish that Duke, Krzyzewski or anyone affiliated with the university has engaged in the conduct he describes.

Singler concludes by again speaking directly to his former coach.

"Coach, you got again former player being mistreated and abused and you ain't doing nothing, man," he says. "Help out."

Third Video Continues Singler's Plea for Help

Singler continues the theme in a third clip, saying that his accounts are "hijacked and frozen" and claiming that people are watching his residence.

He again turns to the coach he addressed throughout the other videos.

"I need your help," Singler says. "I'm locked in my house and I have no freedom anymore."

Near the end, Singler says he has attempted to contact his former coach "many times" and accuses him of being "deflective" and leaving people behind.

articles.title: US Open mixed doubles prize money, format and teams – including Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: The second edition of the new-look mixed doubles tournament at Flushing Meadows takes place this week
articles.body:
The high-profile mixed doubles event at the US Open is underway with several star pairings in action at Flushing Meadows.

Serena Williams , who returned to tennis in June, partnered up with defending men's singles champion Carlos Alcaraz in New York – but the high-profile duo proved no match for Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals.

World No 1 women's player Aryna Sabalenka and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic were the top seeds but lost in the first round, with the all-American pairing of Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz the second seeds.

The Italian doubles pairing of Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori were the defending champions, but also made an early exit.

Here's everything you need to know for the US Open mixed doubles event.

The main draw starts on Tuesday 25 August with the first round and quarter-finals. Play starts at 4pm BST (11am local) on Arthur Ashe Stadium and 3pm BST (10am local) on Louis Armstrong Stadium.

The semi-finals and final will headline a special night session on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday 26 August, starting at midnight BST (7pm local).

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils bt. Alexandra Eala/Felix Auger-Aliassime 4-1, 4-1

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli [4] bt. Taylor Townsend/Alexander Zverev 4-2, 4-2

Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz bt. Erin Routliffe/Lloyd Glasspool 5-3, 4-1

Karolina Muchova/Jakub Mensik bt. Kristina Mladenovic/Marcelo Arevalo 4-1, 2-4, 10-7

Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul bt. Amanda Anisimova/Learner Tien [3] 5-3, 4-2

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev bt. Sara Errani/Andrea Vavassori 1-4, 4-1, 11-9

Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud bt. Jessica Pegula/Taylor Fritz [2] 4-2, 4-1

Svitolina/Monfils bt Siniakova/Patten 5-4, 4-5, 10-8

Bencic/Cobolli [4] bt. Williams/Alcaraz 5-4, 4-1

Muchova/Mensik bt. Navarro/Paul 4-1, 5-3

Andreeva/Rublev vs Shnaider/Ruud 4-1, 4-5, 10-4

For every match up to the final, matches will be best-of-3 sets, with sets to four games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

For the final, it will be a traditional set to six games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

All matches will have sudden death deuce.

Matches in the United Kingdom will be broadcast on Sky Sports Tennis .

In the United States, ESPN2 will present live coverage, with the final on ESPN and ESPN+.

articles.title: Fire in Pakistan hospital nursery kills at least 14 newborns, officials say
articles.summary: A fire at a nursery in a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital killed 14 newborns, hospital officials and the government said.
articles.body:
Islamabad — A fire at a nursery in a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital killed 14 newborns, hospital officials and the government said.

The nursery at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences housed 15 newborns when the fire broke out, hospital officials said. At least one baby was rescued.

Rescue officials said the fire began at about 6:45 a.m., apparently after the compressor of an air-conditioning unit exploded inside the nursery, which is part of the hospital's gynecology ward.

Firefighters quickly responded and extinguished the blaze, and rescue teams were carrying out cooling operations at the site, local media reported.

The ward was cordoned off and ambulances were seen outside the hospital building, a witness told the Reuters news service.

A hospital spokesperson didn't immediately respond to calls from The Associated Press seeking comment.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the deaths and ordered an immediate investigation. A statement from his office confirmed that 14 newborns had died.

"A tragedy involving children is an irreparable loss," Sharif said.

"The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken," he added, according to French news agency AFP.

articles.title: Portage County high school sports recaps for the week of August 24-30
articles.summary: Check out our Portage County high school golf, soccer, tennis and volleyball scores and recaps for the week of August 24, 2026.
articles.body:
Here's a look at Portage County high school sports results from the week of August 24, 2026.

All varsity high school coaches are encouraged to send box scores to sports@recordpub.com.

Watch Ohio High School Sports Live on NFHS Network all year

Photos of Garrettsville Garfield boys soccer vs. Crestwood

The Rovers moved to 3-0-0 behind two goals in the first 127 seconds and a couple of insurance goals in the second half. Senior Zach Pastor ripped the first goal of the game from the left side in the second minute. Exactly a minute later, junior Dylan Boland capped a beautiful run in which he halted, turned inward and then fired away for a 2-0 Rootstown lead. Crestwood hung around the rest of the half, including Owen Overfield's free-kick goal from 35 yards out in the eighth minute. The Rovers finally got the insurance they were seeking in the 54th minute when Bryson Scarlett slotted a perfect pass up to fellow senior Sam Textor for a goal. Pastor added further insurance with his second goal of the game.

Roosevelt 189, Cloverleaf 193, Tallmadge 266

The Rough Riders snapped the Colts' 118-match conference win streak behind junior Brooke Beatty's 39, including birdies on the fifth and eighth holes. Senior Aubrey Byler added a 49 while junior Makenna Ward (50) and senior Coco Golden (51) rounded out the scoring.

Freshman Layla Haynes erupted for four goals to push the Rovers' unbeaten streak to three games. Josie App, Paisley Day and Elliott Smallfield added a goal apiece for Rootstown (2-1-1, 1-0-0 CVC) while Sammy Smolk and Charlie Wilson each tallied an assist.

Brooklyn Wilson scored twice as the Falcons remained undefeated. Molly Murphy added a goal and an assist for Field (4-0-0, 2-0-0 Metro Athletic Conference) while Odessa Hottensmith and Ruby Roberts also scored goals and Peyton Schock added an assist. Zoe Kramer made three saves to record the shutout in net.

Rootstown def. United 25-23, 25-23, 23-25, 25-21

The Rovers had five players record four-plus kills: Lilly Kamenash (seven), Sophi Smith (six), Sophia Byers (five), Alexa Sladky (five) and Ardynn Soika (four). Byers also had eight assists, eight digs and two aces while Kamenash had a team-high three aces. Ella Hayn added a team-high 23 digs for Rootstown (2-0).

Bloomfield def. Windham 25-23, 23-25, 24-26, 30-28, 15-11

The Bombers lost a heartbreaker in which the first four sets were all decided by the minimum two points. Windham fell despite Makenna Jones' 13 kills, Kyleigh Simpson's 11 assists and Kierrah Sanders' 12 digs. Makenzi Blockinger added a stellar performance from the service line with 13 points (including six aces).

The Vikings fell despite two goals from Alexis Henry and two assists from Koralee Jenior. Abigail Roberts had six saves for Waterloo (1-2-0, 0-1-0 Mahoning Valley Athletic Conference), which actually led in both corner kicks (4-2) and shots on goal (15-10).

The Rovers (1-5) fell despite Charlie Wilson firing a 50 and Morgan Giebel tacking on a solid 52.

articles.title: Texas wildfire jumps creeks and rivers as powerful winds drive rapid spread
articles.summary: US News: A fast-moving wildfire in north-central Texas has destroyed a family home and business property, burned buildings at a youth camp and forced evacuatio.
articles.body: A fast-moving wildfire in north-central Texas has destroyed a family home and business property, burned buildings at a youth camp and forced evacuations across sparsely populated ranch country west of Fort Worth, while local ranchers opened barns for animals needing evacuation.The Ross Fire began Monday afternoon and spread across more than 78 square miles (200 sq km) in less than 24 hours, moving through lightly populated areas in two counties. Residents said the blaze crossed creeks and rivers as powerful winds pushed it through ranchland.Firefighters had contained only about 8% of the Ross Fire as of Tuesday evening after high temperatures, dry conditions and gusty winds helped drive its rapid spread, according to the news agency Associated Press.Ranchers open barns for livestockRanchers and a livestock commission made barns available to temporarily hold animals needing evacuation. Emergency centres were opened for residents, while some schools cancelled classes.The blaze also threatened ranch properties around Palo Pinto, where aircraft joined crews on the ground in efforts to protect structures."We've thrown everything at this, and we're still having minimal effect," Fire Chief Danny Watkins said.Family business, century-old home destroyedOutside Graford, the fire hit a business that had been in Katie Rochelle's family for generations.The family's canoe rental operation lost its office and repair shop, while a family home built about a century ago was also destroyed. Some of the company's buses and trailers were also destroyed.Rochelle's husband, a local firefighter, helped protect their home overnight as the fire remained active nearby."I don't know how our house survived," Rochelle said. "Now we're waiting and praying."Buildings destroyed at Worth RanchThe fire also reached Worth Ranch, a youth camp on the southern edge of the affected area, destroying several buildings.Scouting America's Longhorn Council said there were no campers or guests at the property when the flames arrived. All personnel were able to leave safely.Officials in Palo Pinto County had confirmed at least five destroyed structures, although authorities were still assessing the extent of the damage.Federal help mobilised as other Texas fires burnTexas Governor Greg Abbott said resources from the Federal Emergency Management Agency would support firefighting efforts. He also urged residents to avoid activities that could start additional fires during the spell of hot, dry and windy weather.The Ross Fire was not the only blaze demanding attention in Texas. Crews were also responding to four smaller wildfires in surrounding Texas counties.More than 50,000 wildfires recorded across USNational Interagency Fire Center data show that more than 50,000 wildfires have been recorded nationwide this year, the highest number for the same point in the year over the past decade. Twelve new large fires were reported on Sunday alone.In Southern California, areas north of Los Angeles were under a red flag warning through Friday, with forecasters warning that new fires could spread rapidly.In Nevada, authorities sharply reduced evacuation orders around Reno after containment of the Hawk Fire reached 85% by Tuesday evening. The blaze had burned about 23 square miles (60 sq km) and destroyed at least 47 homes.Seven people â three first responders and four civilians â were injured. Fire officials said the Hawk Fire was caused by human activity, though investigators had not determined whether it was deliberately set or accidental.Back in Texas, emergency officials expected the Ross Fire to grow further as temperatures rose.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘We Weren’t Super Emotional’ – Jessica Pegula Details How Her Billionaire Parents Influenced Her Personality
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her par...
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her parents, Terry and Kim Pegula, are co-owners of the NFL's Buffalo Bills and the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, with a combined net worth of $9.3 billion, according to Forbes.

What Jessica Pegula Said About Her Parents' Personalities

Pegula arrived at the US Open on the back of runner-up finishes at the Mubadala DC Open and the Cincinnati Open. Riding on that momentum, the American will be aiming to clinch her maiden Grand Slam title at the New York Major when the singles contest gets underway on Sunday, August 30.

Ahead of her campaign, Pegula sat down with Jon Wertheim for a Sports Illustrated interview in which she offered insight into her personality.

After being praised for her leadership skills, the 32-year-old attributed the quality to her directness and communication abilities, traits she believes she inherited from her mother, Kim, who has been incapacitated since suffering a cardiac arrest in 2022.

"Well, that's a nice compliment. I'm very direct, and I think I'm very honest. But I also think I communicate it pretty well, where it's not taken the wrong way. But I'm definitely pretty direct, and I think I don't know if I got that from my mom," Pegula said .

"I want to say I think she was the same way: very direct with what she thought, and I think [she] was pretty thoughtful in the way she always put things, whether it was to employees or to us or stuff around work. So I think I probably got it from my mom," she added.

The world No. 3 revealed that she and her mother had a different temperament from her father Terry's more emotional personality, saying, "We weren't super emotional. I would say my dad's probably a little bit more emotional. I think my mom and I were definitely more the same personality, like kind of laid back."

In contrast to her laid-back demeanor, Pegula shared that her mind typically races during matches and that she often talks to herself on the court.

"I'm very laid back, but at the same time, I'm thinking a lot out on the court, and so I think maybe some people think I just kind of just go with whatever's happening on the court. But I'm actually thinking quite a bit—like a lot. I talk to myself a lot. I'm constantly running," she said.

"I think when I'm competing—even when I play other sports for fun—I love to just talk to myself and talk myself through things a lot of the time out loud," she added. "And that's where, like my husband, if we're playing golf, he's just like, Just hit the ball. I need to talk through things, so maybe it's a little contradictory with my laid-backness."

articles.title: LeBron James’ LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter-led Guggenheim before joining LA Lakers
articles.summary: Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers, Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company. In 2018, as Jam...
articles.body:
Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers , Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company.

In 2018, as James geared up to sign with the Lakers in free agency, part of his decision to move to the City of Angels was because of his desire to pursue outside business ventures.

Part of this involved setting up a new LLC, which required a massive injection of cash flow. Unbeknownst to him at the time, the man who would end up buying the Lakers seven years later played a crucial part in this.

LeBron James' LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners

According to reporting from Bloomberg , just a few months prior to him signing with the Los Angeles Lakers, LeBron James got into business with future team owner Mark Walter.

In 2018, James' LLC borrowed $300 million from two life insurance companies that were associated with Guggenheim Partners.

At the time, Walter was the CEO of Guggenheim Partners. The amount is due in 2049, allowing James the cash flow his company needed, being leveraged against James' sponsorship and non-NBA earnings.

Furthermore, in 2022, James signed a $97 million contract extension with the Lakers. At the same time, his LLC borrowed more cash from the pair of insurance companies against bonds worth $60 million with an interest rate of 5.75%.

These transactions were approved by the NBA at the time, as they explained in a statement to Fox Business when asked about the matter.

"The 2018 and 2022 transactions were a securitisation done by Mr. James with his personal, non-NBA salary, assets and income, which is a very common financial structure for an individual with this level of earnings and assets.

"Both transactions were fully approved by NBA. Mr. James has no affiliation with Guggenheim, Sammons Financial, North American Life or Midland National beyond their participation in these transactions."

Fast forward to the summer of 2025, and James would become a direct associate of Walter, who purchased the LA Lakers for a then-record $10 billion.

Since James' departure this summer, Walter has sold the Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for a whopping $12.5 billion, amid an investigation into his financial activity.

articles.title: Ziolkowski in talks to join Monza on loan, Parma’s offer for permanent transfer denied
articles.summary: Jan Ziolkowski could leave Roma in the final days of the transfer window. Following the arrival of Koulierakis, the Polish defender, awaiting approval today...
articles.body:
Jan Ziolkowski could leave Roma in the final days of the transfer window.

Following the arrival of Koulierakis , the Polish defender, awaiting approval today for the transfer of Oosterwolde , who can also play in a back three, has fallen to the back row and risks limited playing time this season.

The 2005-born defender is popular with some foreign clubs, but in the last few hours, Monza has moved into pole position, even overtaking Parma .

Roma had inquired about signing Ziolkowski for around €7-8 million, in addition to two foreign clubs who had made official offers to Roma. However, at this price, Roma are now prioritizing a loan move.

In the last few hours, Monza has outbid Parma and two foreign clubs to sign Ziolkowski.

As Fabrizio Romano reports, the Giallorossi are giving priority to the Brianza club, partly because of the terms offered: a loan deal that could allow the 2005-born player to develop and become a valuable asset within a season.

Otherwise, he would be sold in 2027. It is understood that a potential permanent offer outside of the market could reshuffle the cards and change the situation. Further discussions between Roma and Monza are expected today.

This is your one-stop shop for every Dodgers stint on the injured list during the 2026 season. We'll also include every time a player misses time on the paternity list, bereavement leave, or is on the family medical emergency list as well.

Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we'll note it here.

During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list , some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024 , while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL .

Every injured-list stint is a transaction and will also be chronicled on our 40-man roster page . Both are essentially living documents that will be constantly updated throughout the season as these moves happen.

Injured-list stints for pitchers are a minimum of 15 days, and for position players it's at least 10 days.

articles.title: How will Barcelona line up against Athletic?
articles.summary: Hansi Flick’s possible XI for Thursday’s clash
articles.body:
Barcelona look for a strong start to their La Liga home campaign as the reigning back-to-back champions face historic rivals Athletic Club at Camp Nou.

Here's how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Thursday's battle:

Barça got off to an excellent start at the weekend against Elche and now return home where they finished last season with a historic perfect record at Camp Nou, and Flick will be looking to ride the momentum of the team that played so well in the second half on Sunday.

We will likely see only one change at the back since Andreas Christensen needs to be managed carefully and isn't expected to start two games in four days, so Pau Cubarsí will probably make his season debut after his summer glory with Spain.

Gerard Martín is Cubarsí's trusted partner and will start again at center-back, with Eric Garcia picked ahead of Jules Kounde at right-back and young Xavi Espart retaining his place on the left given the fact João Cancelo is still not fully fit and Alejandro Balde 's status is uncertain at best.

Even though Gavi survived an injury scare at the weekend and only suffered a bruise on his knee, it's prudent not to risk him in this one so Pedri will take his place in the lineup alongside Marc Bernal and Fermín López .

We are all excited to see the debut of new signing Rodri that could very well happen in this one, but he's had just a couple of sessions with the squad and will likely come off the bench to get a great ovation from the home crowd in the second half.

Barça's attack put on a show in the second half on Sunday and the noise about the striker position has quieted down for now, especially after Raphinha 's amazing performance as a center-forward. He will start in that spot again, with Karim Adeyemi keeping his place on the left after an excellent competitive debut at the weekend.

Lamine Yamal is very much in preseason form and needs minutes to gain rhythm, so the teenager will start again on the right looking to bounce back from a supbar display against Elche.

Possible XI : Joan; Eric, Cubarsí, Martín, Espart; Fermín, Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Raphinha, Adeyemi (4-3-3)

How do you think Barcelona should line up against Athletic? Let us know your thoughts, predictions and teams in the comments below!

articles.title: Report: Ipswich Town set to land €27.5m World Cup winner
articles.summary: Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels SignificantIpswich Town’s summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and th...
articles.body:
Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels Significant

Ipswich Town's summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and the latest report adds another intriguing layer. According to The Athletic , Ipswich have already moved decisively, with "Ipswich have signed midfielders Sasa Lukic from Fulham and Florentino Luis from Burnley this summer, after Jens Cajuste and Dan Neil departed the club following the conclusion of their loan spells."

That alone tells the story of a club refusing to stand still. Ipswich are refreshing the engine room with experience, physicality and pedigree, and Exequiel Palacios would elevate that strategy again. The 27-year-old arrives in this conversation with serious credentials. As outlined in the report, "Palacios, 27, joined Leverkusen from River Plate in 2020." In that time, "He has made 185 appearances for the club, providing 15 goals and 17 assists, and was part of the side that won the Bundesliga title in 2023-24."

For Ipswich, that sort of background matters. This is not a developmental gamble in the usual sense, it is a player who has operated in title-winning environments and handled the demands of top-level football in Germany and on the international stage. There is, of course, context around his recent availability. "He featured 25 times in all competitions last season either side of four months out with a right adductor injury." That will naturally be part of any assessment, especially for a side looking to add reliability as well as quality.

Still, the ceiling is obvious. "Palacios has been capped 41 times at international level by Argentina." More than that, "He was part of the side that won the 2022 World Cup and was included in the squad for the 2026 tournament but featured just once in the tournament in their final group game against Jordan ." Even limited recent tournament minutes do not diminish the stature he would bring to Portman Road.

From an Ipswich perspective, this would signal intent. Lukic and Florentino Luis suggest structure and control, while Palacios would add craft, composure and proven quality in possession. For a club trying to establish itself and push forward under Gary O'Neil, signing a midfielder with Bundesliga and Argentina pedigree would represent a notable statement.

The attraction here is not only reputation, it is fit. Ipswich needed to respond after losing Cajuste and Neil, and they appear to be targeting players who can immediately raise the standard. If this move progresses, it could become one of the most eye-catching deals of their summer.

As an Ipswich supporter, this is exactly the kind of report that gets you excited. We all knew the midfield needed fresh energy after the loan departures, but bringing in players with this calibre would feel like a major step forward. Lukic and Florentino Luis already suggest the club are thinking bigger, smarter and with real purpose. If Palacios joins that mix, suddenly this midfield has depth, authority and proper top-level know-how.

What stands out most is the mentality he would bring. Anyone who has been around a Bundesliga title-winning squad and an Argentina set-up packed with elite players understands pressure, expectation and quality. That can rub off on everyone around him. At a club like Ipswich, where momentum and belief mean so much, that matters enormously.

There will be some concern over the injury record, and that is fair. Missing four months is not a minor issue. But this is where trust in the recruitment team comes in. If Ipswich believe he is ready and the medical side checks out, then it is easy to see why supporters would back the move.

Most of all, this report feels like confirmation that Ipswich are not here to make up the numbers. These are not timid moves. These are ambitious midfield targets, and fans should embrace that. If the club can land someone of Palacios' profile, Portman Road will believe anything is possible this season.

According to The Athletic , Ipswich have already moved decisively, with "Ipswich have signed midfielders Sasa Lukic from Fulham and Florentino Luis from Burnley this summer, after Jens Cajuste and Dan Neil departed the club following the conclusion of their loan spells."

That alone tells the story of a club refusing to stand still. Ipswich are refreshing the engine room with experience, physicality and pedigree, and Exequiel Palacios would elevate that strategy again. The 27-year-old arrives in this conversation with serious credentials. As outlined in the report, "Palacios, 27, joined Leverkusen from River Plate in 2020." In that time, "He has made 185 appearances for the club, providing 15 goals and 17 assists, and was part of the side that won the Bundesliga title in 2023-24."

For Ipswich, that sort of background matters. This is not a developmental gamble in the usual sense, it is a player who has operated in title-winning environments and handled the demands of top-level football in Germany and on the international stage. There is, of course, context around his recent availability. "He featured 25 times in all competitions last season either side of four months out with a right adductor injury." That will naturally be part of any assessment, especially for a side looking to add reliability as well as quality.

Still, the ceiling is obvious. "Palacios has been capped 41 times at international level by Argentina." More than that, "He was part of the side that won the 2022 World Cup and was included in the squad for the 2026 tournament but featured just once in the tournament in their final group game against Jordan ." Even limited recent tournament minutes do not diminish the stature he would bring to Portman Road.

From an Ipswich perspective, this would signal intent. Lukic and Florentino Luis suggest structure and control, while Palacios would add craft, composure and proven quality in possession. For a club trying to establish itself and push forward under Gary O'Neil, signing a midfielder with Bundesliga and Argentina pedigree would represent a notable statement.

The attraction here is not only reputation, it is fit. Ipswich needed to respond after losing Cajuste and Neil, and they appear to be targeting players who can immediately raise the standard. If this move progresses, it could become one of the most eye-catching deals of their summer.

As an Ipswich supporter, this is exactly the kind of report that gets you excited. We all knew the midfield needed fresh energy after the loan departures, but bringing in players with this calibre would feel like a major step forward. Lukic and Florentino Luis already suggest the club are thinking bigger, smarter and with real purpose. If Palacios joins that mix, suddenly this midfield has depth, authority and proper top-level know-how.

What stands out most is the mentality he would bring. Anyone who has been around a Bundesliga title-winning squad and an Argentina set-up packed with elite players understands pressure, expectation and quality. That can rub off on everyone around him. At a club like Ipswich, where momentum and belief mean so much, that matters enormously.

There will be some concern over the injury record, and that is fair. Missing four months is not a minor issue. But this is where trust in the recruitment team comes in. If Ipswich believe he is ready and the medical side checks out, then it is easy to see why supporters would back the move.

Most of all, this report feels like confirmation that Ipswich are not here to make up the numbers. These are not timid moves. These are ambitious midfield targets, and fans should embrace that. If the club can land someone of Palacios' profile, Portman Road will believe anything is possible this season.

articles.title: Bayern Munich cult hero Luca Toni believes Harry Kane should win the Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Game recognises game. Luca Toni joins the Harry Kane Ballon d’Or train… and so should you. He’s the world’s best.
articles.body:
Yes, that's how we start this segment. An icon in every sense of the word.

With 322 career goals, the Italian football legend and former Bayern Munich star is the fourth most prolific scorer his nation has ever produced. He's won pretty much every individual award as a striker and had a massive role in Italy 's 2006 World Cup win. So yes, the striker role is his bread and butter.

Luca was at the presentation ceremony for the European Golden Boot 2025/26. A trophy won by none other than another Bayern Munich striker… (Sir?) Harry Edward Kane.

During the presentation ceremony, Luca had a couple of iconic things to say (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), with him first requesting Kane to "please stop breaking all our records". For context, no player outside of Lionel Messi has EVER scored more goals in a single season. 73 goals for club and country, with a whopping 61 (!!!) goals for Bayern Munich last season.

Bayern fans certainly want this to continue.

Most importantly, Luca is aboard the Kane Ballon d'Or 2026 hype train. "You deserve to win the Ballon d'Or," concluded the former striker.

Heck, a mic drop would've been perfect. But yes, there you have it. Yet another icon voicing his support for Kane's Ballon d'Or bid. Sure, the award has been a scam for a while now, but surely 81 goal contributions in a single season gets the job done? SURELY???!!!

articles.title: Red Bull Gets Second Chance at Power Unit Upgrade
articles.summary: Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.
articles.body:
Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.

During the last Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) check at the start of the season, Red Bull was found to have the strongest power unit.

There was a full-on bench test, where Red Bull was deemed more than 2% ahead of every other manufacturer, meaning no extra development time, spending, or ability to introduce a new power unit upgrade.

ZANDVOORT, NETHERLANDS – AUGUST 22: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Netherlands at Circuit Zandvoort on August 22, 2026 in Zandvoort, Netherlands. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) // Getty Images

Red Bull fought the assessment directly with the FIA, but in the end, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis and the regulatory body found it a valid conclusion.

"Our measurement, in my opinion, has proven to be very accurate," he said.

"With that said, has everything worked fine? No, because obviously people are not happy and so on. So do we need to think about improvements in the future? Yes, I would say so."

Now, before the Italian Grand Prix, there will be a second ADUO review that could give Red Bull a second chance to get extra development support.

At this point, Red Bull is at best the third-fastest car at most tracks, but usually the fourth- or third-fastest.

An engine upgrade could be what takes their car into race-winning contention.

Max Verstappen | Photo Credit: Red Bull Content Pool

However, Tombazis is not convinced these upgrades are worthwhile or impactful in the grand scheme of things.

"I don't think it would be convenient for you to always be below, just to sort of keep getting more opportunities," he said. "What's the point of opportunities if it isn't ultimately for you to be on top?

"I think the system is working as it was designed. I do think there are some weaknesses that we need to address in the future, for sure, to make it less time-consuming, less controversial. We do need to make some steps to improve it in the future."

Red Bull, while doing a ton of aerodynamic work, begs to differ and will fight for a power unit development opportunity and a chance to challenge the class-leading Mercedes car.

articles.title: Major gangland figure Steven Daniel arrested in organised crime raid
articles.summary: Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel was arrested on Wednesday at his home in the north of Glasgow.
articles.body:
One of Scotland's most high-profile gangland figures has been arrested during an early morning police raid.

Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel, 46 was taken into custody at around 06:00 from his home in Robroyston in the north of Glasgow.

Daniel is understood to be the head of the notorious Daniel crime family which has been engaged in a violent feud with the rival Lyons family for 25 years.

He was arrested in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences as part of Operation Ventetic, a major UK-wide operation which has dismantled several gangs.

BBC Scotland News joined the operation shortly before sunrise.

Dozens of officers involved were briefed at a nearby police station before joining a convoy to Daniel's home.

Two uniformed officers initially approached the property and spoke to him through a first-floor window.

An officer with a police dog then moved in.

Moments later Daniel left the property through the front door and was taken into the back of a police van.

A second man, Steven Gordon, 39 was also arrested in Garthamlock, less than four miles away, in a simultaneous operation.

He was taken into custody in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences and conspiracy to murder.

Assistant Chief Constable Dave Ferry said: "The chief constable has made it clear that those intent on being involved in serious and organised crime will be brought to justice.

"This enforcement action underlines that commitment.

"We will continue to take strong action and to use every tool and tactic available to relentlessly pursue those involved in serious criminality who seek to profit from the harm and misery they cause to communities in Scotland."

The Scottish arm of Operation Venetic has resulted in more than 60 arrests since 2020 when the National Crime Agency penetrated a secret communications system used by criminals.

In May 2017 Daniel suffered serious facial wounds when he was attacked after a 100mph car chase through Glasgow.

articles.title: Fabrizio Romano gives Liverpool fresh hope of landing 18-year-old wonderkid
articles.summary: Liverpool now have around a week left to bolster their ranks. The Anfield outfit are still in desperate need for some new players, especially if they're want...
articles.body:
Liverpool now have around a week left to bolster their ranks.

The Anfield outfit are still in desperate need for some new players, especially if they're wanting to challenge for silverware again.

Some deals such as Bradley Barcola's are edging closer but, at the moment, it's unclear what Andoni Iraola 's squad is going to look like by the time the transfer window slams shut.

The Spaniard was expected to change a lot of things around and, while four of Liverpool's first-team have now left, three have joined but none of them seem to be as good as those that they replaced.

However, fans are still hopeful that the former Bournemouth boss can turn things around this season.

As mentioned, many new players have been linked with a switch but now, the Reds' fanbase have just been given a bit of extra hope in their chase for one long-term target.

Bayer Leverkusen are focusing their attention on Moussa Diaby rather than Ibrahim Mbaye

Replacing Mohamed Salah should have been the first thing on Liverpool's priority list this summer.

Richard Hughes has known since the start of July that Yan Diomande wasn't going to be his man so, that obviously makes fans wonder why signing the Egyptian King's replacement is taking so long.

Barcola is obviously their number one target now and, while he'd be an incredible signing, the fee Paris Saint-Germain are asking for is extortionate and is one of the main reasons why a deal is being held up.

This has caused many other players to be linked with a switch which has then piqued the interest of fans.

Ibrahim Mbaye is one of these other players to have been linked but, since he's 18 years old and has already made a name for himself in Paris, many other clubs alongside Liverpool also want to sign him.

This caused many questions to be raised but now, thanks to an update from Fabrizio Romano, Liverpool's fanbase may be able to breathe a sigh of relief.

"Bayer Leverkusen will now focus their efforts on closing Moussa Diaby deal with Al Ittihad," he wrote .

"Follows green light for Ernest Poku to leave and join Besiktas on initial loan with buy clause."

Liverpool must put everything that they have into strengthening their attack

Since Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur are both lurking to try and prise Cody Gakpo away from Liverpool, some serious changed could be made to the Reds' attack over the next seven days.

On Sunday, Gakpo was Liverpool's best attacker and, on the face of things, it would be silly for them to get rid of the Dutchman at this point in the window.
