articles.title: Bengals wide receiver says he’s fine after limping off practice field
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase said he is fine after suffering a knee injury during Tuesday’s practice.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase said he is fine after suffering a knee injury during Tuesday's practice.

[DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ]

The Bengals wideout raced ahead of DJ Turner II when he reached back to make the catch.

Turner knocked it away, but Chase came down on his left knee, according to Bengals.com.

Dolly Parton dies at 80 after 'brief battle with cancer'

ICE agent charged with shooting in Minnesota could be released from Texas jail

Turner helped Chase off the field. After a few minutes, the Bengals star wideout was seen talking back at defensive backs and trying to get back into practice.

The Bengals medical team ruled him out for the rest of the day.

"I think Cincinnati had a scare (Tuesday)," said Chase. "I missed the ground. I missed my footing, something like that. I sat back down on the ground. I just took a minute to pray, then I got back up. Other than that, I really can't think about anything but God and making sure I'm all right."

Chase said that he would play if the Bengals played tomorrow.

Cincinnati closes the preseason on Friday when they play at Philadelphia at 8 p.m.

articles.title: Islamabad: At least 14 babies die in Pakistan hospital fire
articles.summary: The fire broke out in an air conditioning unit at the mother and child unit in one of Islamabad's main hospitals.
articles.body:
At least 14 newborn babies have died in a fire on a hospital ward in Pakistan's capital Islamabad.

The fire broke out on the third floor of the mother and child unit of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital, one of the main state-run hospitals in the city, on Wednesday morning.

An air conditioning unit caught fire, a spokesman for the hospital told the BBC.

There were 15 babies in the ward when the fire broke out, a hospital spokesman said. One baby was rescued.

The babies in the ward were either in incubators or hooked on oxygen equipment, Pakistan's Health Minister Mustafa Kamal told Geo News. Oxygen is not flammable on its own, but it can accelerate a fire, making materials burn hotter and faster.

Emergency responders rescued at least 19 other people from the hospital, including 10 women, seven children and two men.

The newborn babies who died in the fire have been badly burnt, and will need to be identified in through DNA tests, police said.

Only after the DNA tests can the bodies be returned to their parents.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed his "deep sorrow and heartfelt regret" over the hospital fire, and instructed the authorities to "conduct an immediate investigation", according to the statement from his office.

"Such a situation with children is irreparable", the statement said.

Islamabad's District Magistrate has formed a fact-finding committee to investigate the fire which must produce a report "within 24 hours".

Outside the hospital, one man told the BBC his three-day-old baby had died in the fire.

There was a sense of shock among the families who gathered by the entrance, crying by the side of the ward.

Hivsa Walid told the BBC she was inside the hospital when the fire broke out, with her sister-in-law who had given birth in the days before.

She said they were in the nursery opposite the room where the fire started. They heard a shout and initially thought someone had died but then saw the smoke. They grabbed the baby - who is so young she's not yet been named - and ran.

Police have been patrolling the entrance of the hospital, and the glass from shattered windows lay scattered on the pavement mixed with medical masks.

The PIMS is one of the biggest hospitals in Pakistan's capital, with 156 beds in its maternal and child health unit.

Pakistan has dealt with a number of major fires in recent years, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

In January, a fire ripped through the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Pakistan's largest city of Karachi, killing 67 people.

Pakistan mall fire death toll jumps to 67

articles.title: Teenage cyclist dies after hit-and-run collision at Nugentstown, Kells
articles.summary: A teenager has died after a hit-and-run collision in Nugentstown, County Meath in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.body:
A man in his late teens has died after a hit-and-run collision in County Meath in the Republic of Ireland.

Gardaí (Irish police) said the incident involving a van and a bicycle occurred at about 20:05 local time on Tuesday at Nugentstown, Kells.

They said the van failed to remain at the scene, where the cyclist was pronounced dead.

The coroner has been notified and the road remains closed.

Gardaí have appealed for any witnesses to the incident to come forward and have asked anyone with camera footage, including dash cam or mobile phone recordings, to "make this footage available" to them.

articles.title: Instagram head Adam Mosseri admits few teens used âTake a Breakâ feature before default setting; says âMost teens donât want itâ
articles.summary: Tech News News: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said that only a small percentage of teenagers used Instagram's âTake a Breakâ feature before the company made it a de.
articles.body: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said that only a small percentage of teenagers used Instagram's âTake a Breakâ feature before the company made it a default setting for young users. The feature, which encourages users to step away from Instagram after spending a set amount of time on the app, became a key point of discussion during an ongoing US trial examining whether Meta designed Instagram and Facebook in ways that could make children addicted to them. âMost teens didn't want it,â Mosseri said. âWe decided to push forward with it anyway.âAdam Mosseri said the feature was used by only a low-single-digit percentage of teenagers before Instagram changed its approach in September 2024, nearly three years after launching it.Instagram's 'Take a Break' feature and teen safety under scrutinyAdam Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, testified in a federal court in Oakland, California, as part of a lawsuit brought by 29 US states against Meta. When an attorney representing Colorado questioned him, Mosseri acknowledged that few teenagers had used the âTake a Breakâ feature before it was turned on by default. However, he rejected claims that Instagram deliberately delayed making the safety feature the default option.When the feature was launched in December 2021, Mosseri had said that early tests showed more than 90% of teenagers who turned it on continued using it. The feature encourages users to close Instagram and take a break after a set period.The case is being closely watched as one of the biggest legal tests of social media's impact on young users.US states accuse Meta of designing addictive platformsFour states â California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey â have accused Meta of designing its platforms in ways that could keep young users engaged and contribute to anxiety, depression and suicide. Meta has denied the allegations and said its research found no clear link between adolescents' social media use and a lack of well-being.All 29 states involved in the lawsuit have also accused Meta of improperly collecting and using the personal data of children under 13. The states could seek nearly $200 billion in civil penalties, according to Reuters.Mosseri also denied allegations that Instagram tried to hide information related to children's safety. âI am not trying to encourage my team to hide anything,â he said. âI want to understand how things work. I can't think of any time that I've encouraged people to bring less information to me.âGet the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: UN rejects Israel’s threat to expel Gaza residents over kite-flying
articles.summary: UN rights office spokesperson slams Israeli threat of forced evacuations from Gaza communities over kite flying.
articles.body:
The United Nations has condemned Israel’s threat to expel Palestinians from areas of the besieged Gaza Strip where kites were being flown by children.

“On the threat of expulsion due to children’s kite flying, I hope we can all agree that this is outrageous,” UN rights office spokeswoman Ravina Shamdasani told reporters on Tuesday.

list 2 of 3 No, the Democratic Party is not shifting on Israel

list 3 of 3 Seven killed in Gaza as Israeli strike ‘destroys’ aid supply warehouse

Israel warned Hamas on Sunday that it would intensify military operations if kites, drones or balloons continue, saying those responsible would be targeted.

Several kites not carrying incendiary devices were reported to have drifted into southern Israeli communities over the last month. The incidents have evoked memories of incendiary kites and balloons launched from Gaza in 2018, in what Palestinians said was a protest against the Israeli blockade of the enclave.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz, in a joint statement on Sunday, said “Israel warns Hamas that if the launches toward Israel do not cease immediately”, Israeli forces “will take action to intensify targeted operations against those responsible”. They “will evacuate the population from areas from which kites, drones and balloons are launched”, it added.

Gaza’s popular committees, coordinating with Hamas authorities, urged parents on Monday to stop children flying kites, saying they were acting “to protect their innocent lives”.

“Every summer, my kid, Ahmed, and the kids in the street fly those kites to entertain themselves,” Umm Mohammed, a mother in Gaza City, told the Reuters news agency. “But [now] I will not allow him to – not any more.”

Basem Naim, a member of Hamas’s political bureau, rejected the Israeli warning over the kites.

“Is it conceivable that attempts to appease the war criminal Netanyahu have led them to describe innocent children’s activities as armed activities, while Netanyahu continues to kill and destroy daily despite the agreement?”

The dispute comes amid a “ceasefire” in Gaza that has failed to halt Israeli attacks. More than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed since the agreement took effect in October, according to Gaza’s Ministry of Health.

articles.title: House price growth slows to 3.6% in Q1 FY27, says RBI; whatâs driving the moderation
articles.summary: News News: Indiaâs house price growth slowed to 3.6 per cent year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27, from 4.5 per cent in the previous quarter, indicating a m.
articles.body: Indiaâs house price growth slowed to 3.6 per cent year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27, from 4.5 per cent in the previous quarter, indicating a moderation in the pace of residential property price increases, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data released this week.The RBIâs All-India House Price Index (HPI) rose to 117.5 in Q1 FY27, from 116.2 in Q4 FY26 and 113.4 in the year-ago quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, the index increased 1.1 per cent.While prices continued to rise, the slower annual growth suggests that the sharp momentum seen in some housing markets has eased. The RBI said the latest annual growth was mainly contributed by Chandigarh, Jaipur, Kanpur, Lucknow and Thiruvananthapuram.âThe HPI registered an annual growth of 3.6 per cent in Q1:2026-27, same as in Q1 of previous year, mainly contributed by the cities such as Chandigarh, Jaipur, Kanpur, Lucknow and Thiruvananthapuram,â the RBI said.Why did house price growth slow?The moderation in the overall index came despite continued quarterly gains in several cities. The RBI said the 1.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter increase was primarily driven by Chandigarh, Lucknow and Thiruvananthapuram.âThe All India HPI increased by 1.1 per cent and stood at 117.5 in Q1:2026-27 compared to previous quarter, primarily driven by an increase in the index for cities such as Chandigarh, Lucknow, and Thiruvananthapuram,â the central bank said.The data therefore points to a mixed housing market, with prices continuing to move higher but the pace of annual appreciation remaining modest. The 3.6% annual growth in Q1 FY27 was also unchanged from the corresponding quarter of FY26.The HPI is compiled quarterly using transaction-level data from property registration authorities. With 2022-23 as the base year, the latest index covers 18 major cities, including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad and Gurugram-region markets such as Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar.The index tracks movements in residential property prices based on registered housing transactions across these cities and provides a broad indicator of the direction of Indiaâs housing market.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Big heels, bigger wigs: Dolly Parton’s singular style
articles.summary: The late Dolly Parton often flirted with bad taste, styling plunging necklines with long acrylic nails and heapings of glitter. But she paired it with charm and a keen sense of self-awareness that only made her fans love her more.
articles.body: Adorned in rhinestones and elevating her 5-foot stature with sky-high heels and voluminous blonde wigs, Dolly Parton often joked, “it costs a lot of money to look this cheap!” Parton’s looks on stage and off reflected both her Tennessee roots and her embodiment of over-the-top feminine glamour, an aesthetic articulated in her album title and self-anointed nickname “Backwoods Barbie.” She was rarely seen without long acrylic nails, a full face of makeup, and heapings of glitter. The prolific musician, actor and philanthropist, who died on Tuesday at 80 years old, always had a tongue-in-cheek response to criticisms about her larger-than-life sense of style. She quipped about her hair being a fire hazard, would play her hit ‘9 to 5’ with nothing but her fire red acrylic nails as the instrument, and she unabashedly loved flashy clothes: shoulder pads, plunging necklines, a cinched waist, lace were all sartorial non-negotiables for the singer. But she paired it with a keen sense of self-awareness that only made her devout fanbase love her more. “When I moved to Nashville in 1964, I already had some ideas about what I wanted to look like onstage — and off,” she wrote in her book “Behind the Seams” in 2023. “Country stars had to have big hair and some sparkles, and you had to have a Cadillac. I had the big hair but not yet the Cadillac — or enough sparkles.” She related to the clothes worn by famous fixtures on stage of the Grand Ole Opry, like Jean Shepard and didn’t shy away from the unconventional things that influenced her, telling People she even took inspiration from the famously risqué Frederick’s of Hollywood catalogs she flipped through when she was young. Parton’s version of glamour wasn’t afraid to flirt with bad taste. “I want to look a little bit, you know, trashy,” she said last year. “I don’t mean it in a bad way. I just like that kind of almost artificial look. I like the overdone. I like the bleached hair.” Persuasive style Parton’s conviction was the backbone of her persona, and she recalled in “Behind the Seams” that when she first signed to Monument Records in 1965, the label president wanted to “flatten” her hair and dress her in “streamlined” clothes more fitting of ’60s pop stars. “But I hated everything about it. I felt naked,” she said. Even her softer looks had volume, such as Parton’s cover for her 1973 chart-topping album “Jolene,” in stripes and billowing white shoulders and with her blonde mane framing her face. But on stage and on red carpets she gravitated towards hot pink jumpsuits, icy blue off-shoulder gowns or pearl-encrusted cropped jackets. She worked with designers like Bob Mackie, who created a wing-like “Butterfly” gown for her TV special “Dolly & Carol in Nashville” in 1979, and dressed her and Oprah in complimentary looks for Parton’s variety show “Dolly.” In 2000, she attended a White House luncheon to talk about her book gifting charity Imagination Library in a vibrant, fringed yellow skirt suit with matching heels. Fringe was another Parton trademark. Her looks often incorporated classic country motifs like cowboy hats or bell-bottom jeans, though usually made Dolly-appropriate with a healthy helping of sparkles and vibrant hues. Parton wore some 300 custom outfits a year, styled by her longtime collaborator Steve Summers. He told Vogue that everything was custom for Parton, even if started as an off-the-rack dress. “There is an outfit in production every single day,” he said. “If she’s doing personal appearances, 10 outfits in a day is not unusual.” Many stars have borrowed from Parton over the years: her goddaughter Miley Cyrus has appeared with her in synchronized outfits; Beyoncé has channeled her for her own take on “Jolene;” and Sabrina Carpenter has dueted with her, too, leaning into the unapologetic femininity (and butter-yellow curls) that made Parton an icon. But Parton’s style is something anyone can slip on, and her fans have often played dress-up with her, too. The British photographer Alice Hawkins spent a decade documenting herself and others living out their own Dolly-fied American dreams in her image, published in the book “Dear Dolly” in 2022. Parton even once joined the fun by entering a Dolly lookalike contest at a West Hollywood gay bar — which she lost. “I say it’s a good thing I was a girl or I’d be a drag queen,” she said in an interview recounting the episode. And though guests who make the pilgrimage to her Tennessee theme park Dollywood may not dress as her — per the official rules, since she herself often attended — many still pay small tributes to her style with a touch of glitz. Parton may have had a replicable sartorial style, but the core of it was a message that anyone could adopt, bedazzled or not: “I’m gonna be me, ‘cause I know who I am and you don’t.”

articles.title: In 2024, Marshall Islands crews cleared rats from two remote islands: A year later, 2,000 sooty terns returned
articles.summary: US News: Conservation teams spread rat bait across Bikar Atoll and Jemo Islet in the Marshall Islands using drones in July 2024. A year later, monitoring teams.
articles.body: Conservation teams spread rat bait across Bikar Atoll and Jemo Islet in the Marshall Islands using drones in July 2024. A year later, monitoring teams found a new colony of about 2,000 sooty terns on Bikar and thousands of native tree seedlings across the forest floor. Invasive rats had overrun the two remote islands for years. The rodents ate native vegetation, seabird eggs and young, turtle hatchlings and other wildlife. On Jemo, they also damaged resources traditionally collected by people from the nearby Likiep Atoll. The Marshall Islands government led the restoration effort, with technical support from Island Conservation. By 2025, monitoring indicated that the rats had been successfully removed from both islands.The rats had taken over the forest floorIsland Conservation project manager Paul Jacques visited Bikar and Jemo in 2024, when rats were widespread across both islands. He told CNN that the animals were running through the forest at night and had become a major pressure on native species. The problem was particularly serious for animals that nest or feed on the ground. Rats can eat eggs and young birds, while also consuming seeds and seedlings before they can develop into mature plants.CNN reported that the bait was dropped by drone in July 2024 at a rate of about 25 kilograms per hectare. The pellets were distributed in lines across the islands so that rats would have little opportunity to avoid them. The campaign was carried out with the Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority and the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce. The goal was to remove the invasive predator and allow the existing ecosystem to recover.A new seabird colony appeared within a yearWhen conservationists returned in 2025, they found about 2,000 sooty terns breeding on Bikar. There had been no sooty terns recorded there during the previous year's monitoring. Conservationists also observed greater crested terns and brown noddies nesting on the ground. A Christmas shearwater was recorded on Bikar, while geckos and land crabs that had not been detected during the 2024 visit were also seen.Island Conservation's September 2025 report said the sooty tern colony was feeding hundreds of chicks. The organization described the findings as evidence that the 2024 rat-removal campaign had succeeded. The result is notable because sooty terns are vulnerable to predators when they nest on the ground. Removing rats does not automatically guarantee a population increase, but the new colony appeared during the first year after eradication. The monitoring team used trail cameras, traps, spotlight searches and thermal detection equipment to check whether rats remained on the islands. Those methods supported the conclusion that the rodents had been successfully eradicated.The forest floor changed just as quicklyConservationists found thousands of seedlings of the native Pisonia grandis tree on monitored plots across the islands. In 2024, none had been recorded in the 60 monitored plots. Pisonia grandis is important to island ecosystems because mature trees provide habitat used by seabirds. The sudden appearance of young plants therefore matters beyond the number of seedlings counted. The change also suggests that seeds were surviving after the rats were removed. Before the eradication, rats could consume seeds and young plants before they had a chance to establish themselves.Island Conservation reported that the recovery was documented by teams from the organization, the Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce and community members from Utrik Atoll. The restoration also has a connection to the surrounding ocean. Seabirds carry nutrients from the sea onto islands through their guano, which adds nutrients to the soil, and those nutrients can support plant growth and eventually move back into nearby marine ecosystems. The Marshall Islands' Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme said the 2024 rat-removal project was part of the Predator Free Pacific program, with Island Conservation providing technical expertise. The program involved both Bikar and Jemo and was led locally by Marshall Islands agencies.Jemo could become useful to nearby communities againJemo Islet lies about 40 kilometers from Likiep Atoll. CNN reported that people from Likiep have traditionally traveled to Jemo to fish, collect coconut crabs and gather plants such as coconuts and pandan leaves used for weaving. Those resources had declined as invasive rats became established, and the restoration project was therefore not limited to wildlife protection. paragraphs: Conservation teams spread rat bait across Bikar Atoll and Jemo Islet in the Marshall Islands using drones in July 2024. A year later, monitoring teams found a new colony of about 2,000 sooty terns on Bikar and thousands of native tree seedlings across the forest floor. Invasive rats had overrun the two remote islands for years. The rodents ate native vegetation, seabird eggs and young, turtle hatchlings and other wildlife. On Jemo, they also damaged resources traditionally collected by people from the nearby Likiep Atoll. The Marshall Islands government led the restoration effort, with technical support from Island Conservation. By 2025, monitoring indicated that the rats had been successfully removed from both islands.The rats had taken over the forest floorIsland Conservation project manager Paul Jacques visited Bikar and Jemo in 2024, when rats were widespread across both islands. He told CNN that the animals were running through the forest at night and had become a major pressure on native species. The problem was particularly serious for animals that nest or feed on the ground. Rats can eat eggs and young birds, while also consuming seeds and seedlings before they can develop into mature plants.CNN reported that the bait was dropped by drone in July 2024 at a rate of about 25 kilograms per hectare. The pellets were distributed in lines across the islands so that rats would have little opportunity to avoid them. The campaign was carried out with the Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority and the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce. The goal was to remove the invasive predator and allow the existing ecosystem to recover.A new seabird colony appeared within a yearWhen conservationists returned in 2025, they found about 2,000 sooty terns breeding on Bikar. There had been no sooty terns recorded there during the previous year's monitoring. Conservationists also observed greater crested terns and brown noddies nesting on the ground. A Christmas shearwater was recorded on Bikar, while geckos and land crabs that had not been detected during the 2024 visit were also seen.Island Conservation's September 2025 report said the sooty tern colony was feeding hundreds of chicks. The organization described the findings as evidence that the 2024 rat-removal campaign had succeeded. The result is notable because sooty terns are vulnerable to predators when they nest on the ground. Removing rats does not automatically guarantee a population increase, but the new colony appeared during the first year after eradication. The monitoring team used trail cameras, traps, spotlight searches and thermal detection equipment to check whether rats remained on the islands. Those methods supported the conclusion that the rodents had been successfully eradicated.The forest floor changed just as quicklyConservationists found thousands of seedlings of the native Pisonia grandis tree on monitored plots across the islands. In 2024, none had been recorded in the 60 monitored plots. Pisonia grandis is important to island ecosystems because mature trees provide habitat used by seabirds. The sudden appearance of young plants therefore matters beyond the number of seedlings counted. The change also suggests that seeds were surviving after the rats were removed. Before the eradication, rats could consume seeds and young plants before they had a chance to establish themselves.Island Conservation reported that the recovery was documented by teams from the organization, the Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce and community members from Utrik Atoll. The restoration also has a connection to the surrounding ocean. Seabirds carry nutrients from the sea onto islands through their guano, which adds nutrients to the soil, and those nutrients can support plant growth and eventually move back into nearby marine ecosystems. CNN reported that people from Likiep have traditionally traveled to Jemo to fish, collect coconut crabs and gather plants such as coconuts and pandan leaves used for weaving. Those resources had declined as invasive rats became established, and the restoration project was therefore not limited to wildlife protection. Local communities also have an interest in keeping Jemo free of rats so that its natural resources can recover.Bikar is rarely visited outside scientific expeditions, while visitors to Jemo will need to avoid accidentally bringing rats or other invasive species back. articles.title: HAL, Safran seal engine deal to power multi-role choppers
articles.summary: News News: BENGALURU: Defence PSU HAL and Safran Helicopter Engines have signed the final contract with their joint venture, Safhal Helicopter Engines Pvt Ltd, t.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Defence PSU HAL and Safran Helicopter Engines have signed the final contract with their joint venture, Safhal Helicopter Engines Pvt Ltd, to design and develop a new high-power helicopter engine that will power Indiaâs proposed 13-tonne Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) and its naval variant Deck-Based Multi-Role Helicopter (DBMRH).The engine, Aravalli, named after Indiaâs iconic mountain range, will be developed in the 3,500-4,000 shaft horsepower (shp) class. The contract covers its design, development, manufacture, supply and lifecycle support.The agreement was signed by HALâs director (engineering and R&D) Ajay Kumar Shrivastava and Olivier Savin, director, Safhal Helicopter Engines and executive vice-president (sales and marketing) at Safran Helicopter Engines.âThe signing of this contract marks a significant step forward in Indiaâs pursuit of self-reliance in aero-engine technologies. Through this collaborative programme with Safhal and Safran Helicopter Engines, weâre creating a strong foundation for powering next-generation Indian helicopter platforms,â HAL CMD Ravi K said.Aravalli will be a new-generation turboshaft engine designed specifically for the IMRH and DBMRH. Safran Helicopter Engines chief executive Cedric Goubet said the programme marked a new phase in the partnership between the two companies.âThis is the first time Safran HE has taken up such a class of engine as co-development. The Aravalli engine programme represents a new chapter in the strategic relationship between France and India, combining the expertise of our teams to develop propulsion systems for future Indian rotorcraft,â Goubet said.HAL and Safran have worked together on helicopter engines for decades. Safranâs Artouste engines powered the Cheetah and Chetak helicopters, while the Shakti engine family powers HALâs Advanced Light Helicopter, Light Combat Helicopter and Light Utility Helicopter.Beyond the two military helicopter programmes â IMRH and DBMRH â Aravalli could also find applications in civil aviation, including offshore transport, utility missions and VVIP travel. The programme is also expected to support the development of maintenance, repair and overhaul capabilities in India.The IMRH programme is central to HALâs plans to develop a medium-lift helicopter to meet the requirements of the Indian armed forces, potentially replacing ageing platforms and reducing dependence on imported helicopters and engines.

articles.title: In 1978, Seoul began dumping its rubbish on a river island; 15 years and 92 million cubic metres of waste later, two 98-metre garbage mountains were sealed beneath five ecological parks
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how Nanjido Island in Seoul transformed from a massive landfill into a beautiful ecological park featuring hiking trails and green spaces, following years of waste disposal and remediation efforts.
articles.body: For fifteen years, a small island on the Han River took in almost everything Seoul threw away. By the time the dumping stopped, the site held two mounds of trash nearly a hundred metres tall. What happened next was a slow process of sealing, planting and rebuilding that transformed one of the cityâs most notorious eyesores into a cluster of public parks with football stadiums, hiking trails and silver grass festivals.1978: Nanjido was chosen after Seoul's existing dump sites reached capacity Waste generation in Seoul in the 1970s was outstripping the capacity of existing waste disposal sites. For instance, areas such as Gunja-dong, Sangwolgok-dong and Yeomchang-dong, which have been dumping grounds since 1964, were becoming overcrowded due to the increased population and construction in Seoul. The government sought a site that would be easily accessible by transportation and chose Nanjido Island in the Han River, where wild orchids used to grow. The research on this history, A Study on the Current Status of Landfill in Seoul and the Solutions to Future Generation Landfill Problems, published in the Journal of Wellbeing Management and Applied Psychology, records that dumping at Nanjido ran from March 1978 to March 1993. During this period, Nanjido served as Seoul's primary waste disposal site, though independent verification of the city's exact population served or the precise share of household waste processed was not available.March 1978 to March 1993: 92 million cubic metres dumped to create two 98 metre high moundsNanjido landfill differed from sanitary landfills of today in not being lined, covered, and controlled in terms of pollution control measures. The study also says Nanjido landfill covered 2,720,000 square metres, roughly the same as Yeouido Island, and that the low-lying fill reached 13 metres above sea level at its highest point in December 1985.Thereafter, the Nanjido landfill site was divided into two parts named Noeul Park and Haneul Park, as documented in Seoul Solutionâs official record of the landfill recovery project. Initially, officials set a 45-metre height limit in line with international standards for sanitary landfill sites. However, due to delays in the construction of the new site at Gimpo, Seoul had to continue filling the site with more waste and ended up with the creation of two high mounds, each of a height of 92 to 98 metres high, storing nearly 92 million cubic metres of waste. Living conditions at the dump were so poor that it was dubbed âSamdado,â or the island of three excesses: dust, smell and flies. Almost 3,000 people collected trash there for a living, recycling paper, bottles and cans, but gas from decomposition caused about 1,390 fires during the dumpâs 15 years of operation.1998 to 2002: Impermeable barriers, leachate treatment and 106 gas wellsSeoul closed Nanjido to new waste in March 1993 and turned its attention to containing the damage already done. The stabilization project formally began in January 1998 and was completed in October 2002, a span of nearly five years. It included impermeable walls to keep leachate from seeping into local groundwater, leachate management, methane gas extraction wells, mound stabilization to reduce the risk of collapse, and a soil cover on both mounds to allow vegetation to grow on top of them. Leachate from the facility had contained a Biological Oxygen Demand of 72 mg/l and a Total Nitrogen concentration of 1,416 mg/l, levels which could contaminate the Han River and its associated groundwaterTo address methane accumulation within the mounds, engineers constructed 106 gas extraction wells distributed evenly across the old landfill at 120-metre intervals. The methane was then used to provide heating for three public sites, including the World Cup Stadium, 40 office buildings, and 16,335 households in surrounding residential areas. The volume of energy extracted from 2002 to 2014 also amounted to almost 43.85 million cubic metres, worth more than 8.7 billion Korean won.Post-capping survey finds exotic species dominating the landfill slopesOnce the mounds were capped, the question became whether anything could grow on ground built entirely from buried rubbish. A vegetation and soil survey, The Plant Community of Nanjido, a Representative Nonsanitary Landfill in South Korea: Implications for Restoration Alternatives, published in Water, Air, & Soil Pollution, set out to answer exactly that. The researchers surveyed the landfill and nearby forest controls with 10 Ã 10 m quadrats, then analysed soil pH, conductivity, organic matter, nutrients, and texture before running canonical correspondence analysis. They found that landfill soils were less acidic and significantly richer in P, Ca and Mg and that the slopes were already dominated by tree species such as Salix babylonica, Robinia pseudoacacia and Ailanthus altissima.Tree species that had taken hold on their own included willow, plane trees, black locust, tree of heaven and Korean forsythia, while Mongolian oak, the region's natural late-successional species, was largely absent from the disturbed ground. The study found that invasive and exotic plants were more common where disturbance was greater, soil conditions differed, and more exotic species were already present. The authors recommended introducing native plant stock from similar disturbed sites and limiting further ground disturbance as the more realistic path toward a stable, native-dominated cover.May 2002: Opening of five parks on the former landfill siteAhead of the Korea-Japan World Cup, the parks opened to the public in May 2002, several months before the broader landfill stabilization project was formally completed in October 2002 The five parks make up World Cup Park, built on the former landfill site and adjacent land. Haneul Park and Noeul Park are located on top of the two old garbage heaps, whereas Pyeonghwa Park and Nanjicheon Park are found on the flattened reclaimed land and Nanji Hangang Park is found along the riverside.The project is widely known internationally. According to Seoul Solution, the city received a Special Award from UN-HABITAT and attracts about 3,000 visitors a year from other countries who come to learn about the project. What began as a last-resort response to a waste problem became a 24-year lesson in restoring heavily polluted land. Methane is still being monitored beneath the turf at Haneul Park, showing that the landfill remains active beneath the surface.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Keenan Allen changed Ashton Dulin's role. Now the Colts may use him everywhere.
articles.summary: Veteran Ashton Dulin has been the Colts' No. 2 healthy receiver in training game but may drop to No. 4, opening up roles on special teams.
articles.body:
Brian Mason has never been shy in his views of Ashton Dulin 's performance on special teams, calling the 29-year-old receiver veteran "one of the three-best special teams players in the NFL" last fall.

How much the Colts will be able to take advantage of those skills – on his most active days, Indianapolis uses his 4.4 speed as its primary gunner on punt coverage, as well as one of its two returners on kickoffs – may vary week-to-week, depending on the team's health across the board.

After last week's signing of six-time Pro Bowl receiver Keenan Allen , Dulin finds himself no longer in contention for one of the Colts ' three starting wideout spots. Instead he's jockeying with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine for fourth on the depth chart on a team whose star second-year tight end Tyler Warren makes Dulin or Westbrook-Ikhine the fifth receiving option at-best.

NFL preseason; Indianapolis Colts against Atlanta Falcons

Dulin has performed arguably the most consistently of Indianapolis' rotational wideouts in the preseason, all while taking very few reps on special teams. It gave the appearance the Colts planned to significantly reduce his role on punt and kick teams to preserve his energy and impact for offense. But with Allen's signing dropping Dulin a spot, the receiver who has just seven catches since the end of the 2022 campaign finds himself in virtually the same spot as the end of last season.

"How many phases and plays he gets on special teams will just be dictated by how many plays (the offensive coaches) anticipate him getting in a game," Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason told reporters Monday. "We usually meet at the beginning of a regular season game week, and we'll kinda project who'll be up for the week and how much they plan to play.

"If they say, 'He's going to play this number of plays' on offense, that will then determine whether he plays in one, two or three phases on special teams."

As Mason went on to explain, the Colts plan to look at Dulin as a potential punt returner this week, among a long list of kick return spots. Among players in the NFL in 2025 with more than one kickoff return attempt, Dulin's 32.3-yard average ranked third-best in the league, but in the background, Mason said Dulin has been working on his punt return skills for two years.

Through two preseason games, second-year receiver Coleman Owen has been the Colts' most consistent and active returner on kicks and punts, with rookie running back Seth McGowan and rookie receiver Deion Burks , shuffling through in preseason action. Incumbent starting returner Anthony Gould has been out for much of camp with a groin injury, while the team lost frequent returner Ameer Abdullah in free agency. Josh Downs has taken reps on punt return, but the team would like to limit that given his increasing role in the offense.

Mason went on to explain that Dulin's lack of special teams reps throughout training camp came, in part, so the team could evaluate its young fringe roster players to narrow in on final contenders for various roles he would be a finalist for, pending his responsibilities on offense.

"We planned on using Ashton Dulin in roles no matter what, whether that be on kick return or at gunner. If he ever needs a sub at gunner, we can always give him a sub, but we certainly still want to have the threat of being able to use him and our opponent knowing there's a good chance he still may be out there," Mason said. "I think that does affect certain people's punt return game plan.

"If Ashton Dulin is on the field for the punt team, you certainly have to account for him and you certainly need to probably (double-team) him in order to prevent him from causing problems."

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter .

articles.title: 'Just fantastic with people.' Tom O'Brien had a lifelong connection with Cathedral
articles.summary: Tom O'Brien was coaching at the college level in 1967 when he came back to coach at Cathedral, his alma mater. He maintained longtime connection.
articles.body:
Tom O'Brien was a college basketball assistant at Bradley in 1967 when the opportunity arose to come back to coach at Cathedral, his alma mater.

O'Brien would leave a couple different times as coach, but never really did give up his connection to the school where he graduated from in 1949. O'Brien died on Aug. 17 at age 95.

"Tom had such a history with Cathedral, graduating from there and all the changes the school went through in good times and bad times, Tom was always part of it," said Steve Hodgson, who coached with O'Brien and then later succeeded him. "It goes even beyond that. There are so many families in the Catholic and Eastside community and people that I've heard from in the last week through Tom's passing that he touched."

O'Brien not only coached football, basketball and baseball at Cathedral, he later returned as a substitute and earned the nickname "Super Sub."

"Tom left a profound impact on Cathedral, both as a student and when he returned as an educator and coach," Cathedral shared on its social media accounts. "'Coach OB' coached football, basketball and baseball at Cathedral, leaving a lasting legacy on thousands of Cathedral students. During the final years of his tenure at Cathedral, he was affectionately known as 'Super Sub,' and students were always thrilled to see him walk through the classroom door."

O'Brien, who played football at Butler for legendary coach Tony Hinkle, coached on the staff at Evansville College for Arad McCutchan, helping the Aces to a perfect season in 1964-65. That team was led by Larry Humes and Jerry Sloan. But after coaching at Evansville and Bradley, O'Brien was drawn home with the opportunity to coach basketball at Cathedral.

After leading Cathedral to a 71-27 record over a four-year period, including the program's first sectional championship in 1971, O'Brien also served as the Marion County Clerk from 1975-79 before he was rehired as Cathedral's coach in 1979.

"He was a really, really good coach," said Brad Lennon, who was hired as O'Brien's freshman team coach in 1980 and coached on his staff the next six seasons. "He wasn't necessarily a master technician but he was a players' coach. He had a heart of gold and would do anything for anybody – just fantastic with people."

Steve Hodgson remembered one afternoon when O'Brien was feeling sick and was not going to be able to make it to a game at Center Grove. He spent 45 minutes talking on the phone to Hodgson, his assistant at Cathedral, about the game plan for the night. Just before the tipoff, O'Brien showed up at the game, saying he was "feeling better and coming to support the kids."

"I turned to Brad and said the over/under on him sitting on this bench is halftime," Hodgson said with a laugh. "I missed it by a quarter. If he was there, he was going to coach. I'd probably be the same way."

O'Brien's best team was the 1981-82 group led by senior Ken Barlow and junior Scott Hicks, both of whom would go on to Notre Dame; Shelton Smith (Wisconsin) and Carl Daniels (Rice). Cathedral was 27-2 going into the Final Four but ran into a buzzsaw in Scott Skiles and Plymouth, falling 62-59 in the afternoon game. Plymouth would beat Gary Roosevelt 75-74 in double overtime for the state championship that night.

"It was a tremendous experience for the kids to play in a packed Market Square Arena," Hodgson said. "We were probably the proverbial favorites. I remember in the locker room after the game, Tom talked to the kids about how it was one day in their lives. He told them they had an incredible season and were able to go to the Final Four ... all the great things they accomplished. Even though he was heartbroken and we all were, I appreciated those comments."

O'Brien stepped down in 1984. He coached nine seasons total at Cathedral, compiling a 164-60 record. He would go on to coach at Blackford in 1986 after two years working in the Marion County Sheriff's Department. O'Brien would later be a Sagamore of the Wabash recipient and an inaugural member of the Cathedral Circle of Excellence. On his 80th birthday, Mayor Greg Ballard declared it "Tom O'Brien Day" in Indianapolis.

"I might not have gotten into coaching if it wasn't for OB," Lennon said. "He was really good about letting you have your two cents as an assistant coach. Just a great guy with a great sense of humor. I owe him a lot."

O'Brien is proceeded in death by his wife, Marilyn O'Brien, his parents, five brothers James, Robert, Jack, Michael, Bernard and sisters Mary O'Brien and Patricia Norton. He is survived by his daughters, Dorothy (Pete) Miller, Kathleen Allgood and sister Barbara (Joseph) Minatel as well as many nieces and nephews.

Visitation will be held on Wednesday from 4-8 p.m. at Feeney-Hornak Keystone Mortuary, 2126 E. 71st Street. A Mass of Christian Burial will be held on Thursday at 11 a.m. at St. Lawrence Catholic Church 6944 E. 46th Street, with burial to follow in Westridge Park Cemetery.

Memorial contributions go to Cathedral Tuition Assistance Fund, 5225 E. 56th St., Indianapolis, IN 46226.

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight this weekend
articles.summary: Young British sensation Moses Itauma boxes Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF heavyweight title
articles.body:
This weekend, Moses Itauma will fight Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF heavyweight title, with a piece of history on the line.

If Itauma wins, the Briton will become the youngest world heavyweight champion since Mike Tyson , who broke the record 40 years ago.

And Itauma, 21, will enter Saturday's main event full of confidence, with a 14-0 (12 KOs) record to his name, having stopped Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin in his last two bouts.

Hrgovic is a seasoned heavyweight, however, an Olympic medalist who has lost just once as a pro. The Croatian, 34, was bloodied by Daniel Dubois to the point of a stoppage in 2024, but he has since beaten three Britons in a row.

Will Itauma be the fourth? Or can the young star claim his biggest scalp yet? As he and Hrgovic vie for the IBF belt, after Oleksandr Usyk vacated it this summer, here's all you need to know.

Itauma vs Hrgovic will take place on Saturday 29 August at the O2 Arena in London. The main card is due to begin at 6.30pm BST (10.30am PT / 12.30pm CT / 1.30pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at approximately 10pm BST (2pm PT / 4pm CT / 5pm ET).

Itauma vs Hrgovic and its undercard will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view, at a cost of £24.99. You can purchase the fight here , which also allows eight free days of DAZN Standard.

articles.title: Report: Liverpool star still has two Premier League suitors
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest as Tottenham and Manchester City Monitor Liverpool ForwardThe latest transfer discussion from Fabrizio Romano placed Cody Gakpo fi...
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest as Tottenham and Manchester City Monitor Liverpool Forward

The latest transfer discussion from Fabrizio Romano placed Cody Gakpo firmly among the key late-window stories, with Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City both mentioned in connection with the Liverpool forward.

With the market entering what Romano described as "24 crucial hours", the focus around Gakpo is now on Liverpool's position and whether any movement on incoming wide players changes the picture before the window closes.

Romano set the wider context by saying, "The market is moving things are happening and so it's going to be absolutely busy in the next days." He also stressed the timing, adding, "And also important to mention in seven days the window is closed and so it's going to be very important to see what happens in this hours."

Gakpo agreement with Tottenham already in place

The clearest update in the discussion concerned Tottenham's work on the player side. Romano said, "Talking about Gakpo guys. I maintain my information. He has an agreement on personal terms with Tottenham since July."

He then reinforced that stance by adding, "So Tottenham have an agreement with Gakpo and Tottenham are ready to give Gakpo what he wants."

That is the central detail in this story. According to Romano's information, Tottenham's groundwork with Gakpo has already been done for some time. The personal terms side is not being presented as an issue, and the London club are described as prepared to meet the player's expectations.

At this stage, that leaves the club-to-club element and, crucially, Liverpool's own decision-making as the key part of the situation.

Manchester City also in contact over Cody Gakpo

Romano also revealed that Manchester City have entered the conversation, though with a more tentative position at present.

That distinction matters. Tottenham are being described as having an agreement on personal terms, while City are framed as having held talks with the player's representatives without reaching any agreement.

Romano summarised it directly: "So let's maintain Tottenham there and then Manchester City also meeting with the agents."

In other words, Tottenham remain the more advanced suitor on the information provided, while Manchester City are in the background with contact made and the situation still open.

Liverpool stance depends on two winger arrivals

That is the condition around any potential departure. Romano then spelled it out even more clearly, saying, "If if Liverpool can get two wingers, Gakpo can go to Tottenham or to Man City."

He returned to the same point once more, underlining the threshold Liverpool would need to meet before authorising a sale: "And then it's important to mention that for Liverpool it's two wingers or no chance to give the green light."

From the discussion, there is no suggestion that Liverpool have already approved an exit. The message is that the situation is contingent. Gakpo's future, as Romano explained it, hinges on Liverpool securing two wingers. Without that, the green light does not arrive.

This leaves the story finely balanced in the final stretch of the window. Tottenham have an agreement with the player. Manchester City have spoken to his agents. Liverpool, however, remain the gatekeepers, and their stance is tied to recruitment.

Late-window picture becoming increasingly urgent

As Romano put it, "So many things are happening guys." In Gakpo's case, the essentials are straightforward. Tottenham are advanced on personal terms. Manchester City have made contact with the player's camp. Liverpool's approval depends on signing two wingers.

For now, that means no definitive conclusion has been reached. Yet the framework around the deal is now clear from Romano's update. "Tottenham have an agreement with Gakpo. Man City at the moment not yet. Let's see if they can agree."

Until Liverpool decide whether they can complete the required winger business, Gakpo remains one of the standout stories to watch in the closing days of the window. With Romano emphasising that the market is moving quickly and that the deadline is now close, this is a situation that appears set to run deep into the final stages.

articles.title: Nepal flash flood kills eight; damages roads, power projects
articles.summary: cNepal sent helicopters to the rescue on Wednesday after a massive flash flood swept away villages in the Himalayan nation, killing eight and damaging roads, bridges and power projects in areas near Tibet, authorities said.
articles.body: Nepal sent helicopters to the rescue on Wednesday after a massive flash flood swept away villages in the Himalayan nation, killing eight and damaging roads, bridges and power projects in areas near Tibet, authorities said. Across the border, Tibet reported “major casualties” with some missing in the neighbouring county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a land crossing between China and Nepal, the Xinhua official news agency said. The waters were too high for helicopters to land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, with a population of about 50,000, officials said, while flagging the risk of casualties. “There could be heavy casualties or loss of property,” district administrator Narendra Pariyar told Reuters. “But I cannot say for sure now.” Pariyar urged those living on the banks of the Bhote Koshi river in the area to seek higher ground, pointing to reports that nearby villages and infrastructure project sites were washed away. “It all came suddenly,” the Onlinekhabar portal quoted a witness from the area as saying. “We heard a loud sound, like a volcano erupting. People started to scream and ran away.” Nepal’s rescue helicopters would be unable to land in the affected areas until the waters recede, however, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said. The cause of the inundation was not immediately clear, but a deadly flash flood on the same river last year was eventually traced to the draining of a glacier lake. China says Gyirong port affected The mudslide on the Nepali side hit China’s Gyirong port, Xinhua added, cutting off roads, communications and power in the Shigatse region near the border with Nepal, it added, without giving details. President Xi Jinping urged “all-out” search efforts for the missing as well as stronger monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary disasters. Nepal’s energy ministry said 430 MW of electricity supplies were affected, mostly from hydroelectric projects, or more than 12% of total national hydropower capacity of 3.2 GW, a Reuters calculation showed. Prime Minister Balendra Shah said police and military were joining rescue and relief teams. “Instructions have been given … to move the people living in the lower areas to safer places,” he said. “People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert.” From its origins in Tibet, the Bhote Koshi river empties into Nepal’s Trishuli river that eventually flows into India as the Gandak river. Last year’s Bhote Koshi flood killed nine people, with 24 missing, as it washed away a ‘Friendship Bridge’ linking Nepal and China to disrupt trade and transport for months. That flood was triggered by the draining of a supraglacial lake in Tibet, a regional climate monitor said.
